The smoke of Waterloo has settled, and the ideals of the French Revolution are believed to have vanished with the joint efforts of European monarchs. After the upheavals of the Napoleonic Wars, European nations reached agreement at the Congress of Vienna, temporarily re-establishing peace on the long-troubled European continent. However, although the fires of revolution have been extinguished, the ideas of human rights, nationalism and liberalism will prove to be still alive and well. In the Americas, these same ideals brought a young republic to the brink of a devastating civil war. Princess Victoria is 16 years old, and she is about to ascend the throne as Queen of Great Britain, head of the most powerful industrial empire in the world. Victoria will usher in an era of lasting prosperity and progress, all the way until the outbreak of the First World War. In this era of unprecedented technological development, people will doubt what their ancestors believed for generations, and new doctrines will emerge. Across the oceans, in the rich lands of Asia and Africa, dark corners of the world, they strive to make their voices heard in the concert of European powers. Choose your instrument and begin to play the melody of the era!

Liquor is a popular alcoholic beverage among the masses, produced from grain.
Wine is a status symbol of the wealthy, produced from fruit.
Logs can be made into wood. Wood can be used to build buildings, make paper, build ships and manufacture furniture.

The people are angry about lost territories and such events, they need this Chaplinesque character to cheer them up.

The Freikorps are revolutionaries driven by the new ideology of fascism. Through organized mass violence, the revolutionaries will overthrow the old monarchic order and the new democratic order alike, replacing them with the absolute rule of a fascist leviathan.

The Red Guards are communists in open revolt against the government and, more importantly, against the reactionary pretenses of the bourgeois state and society. Through fighting the establishment of religion, tradition, private property and family, these revolutionaries seek to establish the "dictatorship of the proletariat" as the first step on the long and bloody road to the stateless utopia promised by communism.

The Civic Guards are combative liberals who have risen up against the oppression of the state machinery, whether real or perceived, and will stop at nothing to defend their personal liberties. Through fighting the autocratic state, these revolutionaries consider themselves to be true fighters for freedom.

Reactionary rebels yearn for the so-called good old days. Whether they are absolute monarchists or simply opposed to modern ideologies, you will find these counter-revolutionaries on the front lines against socialism and liberalism.

Pan-Nationalist rebels seek to create a free and independent national state together with their perceived cultural brethren. Spurred on by romantic nationalist movements, they fight for what they consider their homeland and become thorns in the side of peace and order.
Nationalist rebels seek the freedom of their nation. They are well-led and armed, and their goal is the independence of their people.
Patriot rebels dream of unifying their homeland under one free flag. Provinces they occupy will defect to their fellow countrymen's state.
Partisans fight against the occupying forces of a foreign land, their dream is to drive the invaders from their homeland.
They are a mob of disgruntled citizens gathered together, their goal is nothing more than looting and smashing.

Through direct or indirect means we control the principalities, duchies and free cities that make up the German nations, and now the German people can be united in a single nation state. Three cheers for the German Empire!
Having established dominance in the struggle for the Italian peninsula, we can now declare the unification of Italy and guarantee the security of the Italian people and national territory.
For the Welfare of Brotherly Peoples!

Having gained a dominant position in the Scandinavian peninsula, we have the ability to unite the Scandinavian people under one banner. To do this, we must bring the entire Scandinavian peninsula into our kingdom or into our sphere of influence. For the welfare of brotherly peoples!

Decades have passed since the Swedish defeat in the Finnish War, and Finland, the eastern half of the Swedish Kingdom, still temporarily languishes under the Russian eagle. Although intelligence shows that a significant portion of Finland is dissatisfied with Russian rule, not many yearn for reunification with the Swedish Kingdom, preferring independence and autonomy instead. Some believe it is time to abandon the idea of returning Finland to the Swedish Kingdom.
Gag Rule in the House of Representatives

The debate over the continuation of slavery seems increasingly irreconcilable, and our country is in danger of splitting apart. If we introduce a gag rule in the House of Representatives to prohibit bills regarding slavery from being presented on the floor, it might at least de-escalate the current tense situation.

Senators Henry Clay and Stephen A. Douglas have drafted a compromise bill on slavery, which, based on the principle of popular sovereignty, determines the fate of slavery in new territories. If we support this bill, we can to some extent alleviate the current tension over the slavery debate.

Tensions over slavery have reached a boiling point. If we can get Congress to pass the constitutional amendment proposed by Senator Thomas Corwin, it would prohibit Congress from passing any constitutional amendment regarding slavery. This is a desperate measure, but the situation does not allow us to dawdle.

Once we pass the federal fugitive slave act, we must force escaped slaves in free states to be returned to their slaveowners in slave states. Doing so may at least temporarily alleviate the fears of the southern states regarding the abolitionist movement.

Several southern representatives have spoken out against the voices of secession coming from more radical circles. If we informally reach an agreement with these representatives, they may be able to calm the separatists down.

The Ostend Manifesto aimed to annex Cuba and admit it to the Union as a slave state, thereby balancing the free states newly admitted from the west. If we support this manifesto, we can alleviate the current tension in the domestic slavery debate, but it will also greatly weaken our international standing and relations with European great powers.

If we pass the Kansas-Nebraska Act, we effectively repeal the 1820 Missouri Compromise, allowing residents of the old Louisiana Colony (including Louisiana and several states derived from it) to decide for themselves whether slavery should exist there. Abolitionists will hate us for this act, but it is necessary to preserve the integrity of our Union.

Congressman David Wilmot proposed a bill to permanently ban slavery in the newly conquered Mexican territories (including California and New Mexico). Supporting this proviso will greatly alleviate northern fears about slavery, but will increase southern fears about abolitionism.
Apply for Statehood in the USA

Our location on the North American continent and our traditional culture are closely tied to the United States, so it is likely that the USA will agree to our application for statehood. Of course, doing so also means we will be annexed by the USA.
It has been our great and sacred mission as a nation to bring the light of civilization from the East Coast to illuminate the shores of the West. Let the American eagle spread its wings!

We do not have to fire a shot or strike a blow; if they declare war on us, we can tie the entire world to our chariot. Can you imagine a world without cotton for three years? Britain will stagger, and they will have to do their utmost to lead the entire civilized world to save our South. — James Henry Hammond\n\nIf we use this "King Cotton" strategy, we will refuse to export cotton to European nations, which will give the great powers reason to help us in this civil war.

I have been shown in the files of the War Department a statement of the Adjutant General of Massachusetts that you are the mother of five sons who have died gloriously on the field of battle. I feel how weak and fruitless must be any word of mine which should attempt to beguile you from the grief of a loss so overwhelming. But I cannot refrain from tendering to you the consolation that may be found in the thanks of the Republic they died to save. I pray that our Heavenly Father may assuage the anguish of your bereavement, and leave you only the cherished memory of the loved and lost, and the solemn pride that must be yours to have laid so costly a sacrifice upon the altar of freedom. — Abraham Lincoln\n\nBy sending this letter to Mrs. Bixby, we can gain more war support.

The Anaconda Plan was a strategy designed to blockade Confederate ports and weaken their economy to the point of surrender without battle. The plan was devised by General-in-Chief Winfield Scott. The specific plan is to weaken the Confederate economy by blockading major southern ports
column3: then seize the Mississippi River to cut off the South. By executing this plan, we can deny the South the war materials they need to continue the war.

column2: The Federal army is executing the Anaconda Plan proposed by Winfield Scott and is blockading our ports. If they succeed, our war materials will soon run out, pushing us into the abyss of defeat. We must defend the safety of our ports!

During the campaign in Georgia from November to December 1864, Major General William Tecumseh Sherman used so-called "total war" tactics—a series of terrorist acts against southern civilians. By penetrating Confederate territory and destroying much of Georgia's civilian infrastructure, Sherman claimed this would destroy the South's will to fight. His action tolled the death knell for the Confederacy.
Since we control Luxor, we can send an expedition to the Valley of the Kings to conduct archaeological excavations. Discovering the tombs of ancient Egyptian pharaohs would enhance our prestige.

Egypt's Valley of the Kings is a new and exceptionally valuable excavation site for archaeology. By proposing to the Egyptian government a monopoly on excavations in the Valley of the Kings, we can ensure that it is we, not some other great power, who discovers these stunning ancient relics.
Some believe that our nation's experiment with prohibition has lasted too long, and that this excessive constraint should be repealed.

The Prohibition League, an organization dedicated to publicizing the dangers of alcohol abuse and advocating for the prohibition of alcohol, is lobbying policymakers to enact a national decree banning the sale, consumption, and possession of alcoholic beverages. While opponents argue that prohibition will drive the entire alcohol market underground and provide funding for criminal organizations, the Prohibition League believes alcohol is the root cause of many social problems and even the primary cause of crime.

The Great Trek refers to a massive migration of Dutch farmers (Boers) from the Cape Colony, which had come under British control, to lands beyond the Orange and Vaal rivers, eventually reaching the "Boer Republics" established by their relatives in the South African hinterland.

Those white people (called "Boers" among themselves) have crossed the Nkomo River and begun migrating east and west from the British Cape Colony. We have seen them come, with their wives and children, and we suspect they mean to stay, but this land is our land...
By determining the border between our country and the British Cape Colony, we can strengthen relations with Britain.
By determining the border between our country and the British Cape Colony, we can strengthen relations with Britain.

For some time, Hungarian nobles have been pushing for the so-called independence of the Hungarian people and the "Lands of the Crown of Saint Stephen." To this end, a compromise bill with the Hungarian nobles was born, in which the Kingdom of Hungary and the Austrian Empire would merge into a new political entity: the Austro-Hungarian Empire. God save, God protect!

Since we have control over the formerly French territories of Alsace-Lorraine, perhaps it is time to consider renaming the local places. Let us begin to establish the new Imperial Province of Elsass-Lothringen!
Since Alsace has returned to the embrace of its rightful government—France—we can now restore the local place names to their original French forms.

The "Trail of Tears" comes from the Cherokee term referring to the forced relocation of the large Cherokee nation from the southeastern United States (Georgia, Tennessee, Alabama, etc.) to the newly established Indian Territory in Oklahoma. The specific decision to enact the 1830 Indian Removal Act is now in our hands.

The Black Hills, as part of the Dakota Territory, have been recognized by our government as Sioux land. However, this land has not been surveyed for minerals, and recent reports have surfaced that Indians have dug large amounts of gold from the hills. George Armstrong Custer, a young and capable lieutenant colonel, is ready to be sent to the Black Hills to investigate this matter.

In 1862, President Abraham Lincoln passed the Homestead Act, granting eligible applicants up to 160 acres of land in the western United States. This act, along with a series of similar acts, helped establish America's image and reputation as a land of opportunity and new beginnings.

This was originally an internal memorandum handed by King William I of Prussia to the Prussian Prime Minister Otto von Bismarck. The content mainly concerned some demands made by the French ambassador during an informal meeting between the French ambassador and William I at the Bad Ems spa in Hesse-Nassau. The Ems Dispatch was likely the most important trigger for the French declaration of war, which led to what would later be known as the "Franco-Prussian War." By sending the Ems Dispatch, we will risk provoking a war with France.

One hundred years have passed since France and General Lafayette gave their aid during the birth and most dangerous hours of the brave and young United States of America. Since then, America has been a beacon leading all freedom-loving people in the world, clearly expressing to the world the possibility of human freedom. Some French Republicans suggest we should give the American people a suitable gift to celebrate the centenary of their nation and their traditional friendship with France. Long live freedom!

The Germania Shipyard in Kiel has always been a major shipyard in northern Germany, responsible for providing submarines for the German Navy during World War I and World War II, and even including the yacht of Kaiser Wilhelm II. The yard was originally founded in 1867 by the North German Shipbuilding Industry Association, then purchased by the famous German industrialist Friedrich Krupp in 1902 and renamed "Friedrich Krupp Germania Shipyard." By building this shipyard in Kiel, we can ensure we will not lack the ships we need in the future.

Our people's dependence on alcohol is growing day by day, and a tense atmosphere is spreading across the country. Under these circumstances, it is crucial that we take action to uphold our noble social virtues, in the name of our nation's noble and devout character, to resist the onslaught of alcohol, and to bring this good practice to the lower strata of our society.\n\nAlcohol consumption in our country has been increasing steadily over the years. The combined effect of this cheap and readily available distilled spirit, together with harsh working conditions, has naturally led the poorer classes to accept and become addicted to this deadly poison. It is no wonder that the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Prohibition Alliance has emerged.
What harm can a few drinks do? *burp*

Another tavern has opened in this province today, further cementing its reputation as a paradise for vagrants and gamblers. On average, there is one saloon or tavern for every hundred citizens, providing them with venues to indulge in their vices. Although the soul may be saved from even the most desperate circumstances, we cannot ignore the serious consequences of long-term excessive consumption.
Pressure the local authorities to shut it down.

Local residents, angered by the police decision to close the bar, joined by many drunkards in the protest, marched almost riotously through the city streets.

A series of social problems such as poverty caused by alcohol addiction have become increasingly serious in $PROVINCENAME$ and the entire $STATENAME$. They call themselves Socialists and insist that the working class should govern the country, with workers themselves controlling the means of production. We demand, no, we need a free society in which no one is superior to anyone else, no one is abandoned, and no one is exploited or lacks food, clothing, or shelter. We need a society without government, a society without class divisions, a society where workers themselves control the means of production.

How many private clinics are forced to close each year due to open competition? How many pharmacies suffer the same fate? How much individual initiative does our inefficient government bureaucracy sacrifice each year? How many other problems will emerge before we liberalize our health care?\n\nToday a speech in parliament opposing reform drew public attention, and a large crowd of opponents took to the streets to protest the current health care system. How should the government respond?

He lives in a house, a very big house, in the countryside.\n\nAs our city centers grow, rural people flood into the cities. Not surprisingly, there is also an opposite trickle. Due to overcrowding, pollution and substandard housing, urban living and sanitary conditions have deteriorated. This has led some people (mainly from the middle class) to begin to long for the peaceful rural life again. Also, as living standards and wages rise, more people can afford occasional trips out of the city, breathing fresh air and enjoying leisure and recreation in the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ countryside.

Yes, I'd say they feed the pigs better than we eat.\n\nA scandal in one of our regions has attracted nationwide attention in recent weeks. Apparently, a foreman at a local poorhouse embezzled funds, and to make up for it only provided low-quality food to the employees of the facility, sometimes just a few slices of bread a day. Conservatives and liberals have sharply opposing views on this incident
column3: conservatives oppose government intervention while liberals emphasize the need for further social reform.

column2: Hope this matter will be forgotten on its own

Alongside the few voices in society supporting further social reform, some citizens in one of our regions have established an organization called the "Quaker Society" to begin taking in people from the lower strata of society. The organization aims to carry out various social welfare work, including distributing free food to the elderly, providing job opportunities, and religious education for the poor. In addition, the organization operates a poorhouse for this purpose.
This is the individual initiative I'm talking about!
Why is this on my desk?

Thus, the thousands of new deaths this year can be attributed to the rampant tuberculosis in our region.\n\nA physician has privately published a report discussing health care conditions in his hometown. His report has caused a small stir in $COUNTRY$. The report, while generally stating that unsanitary and crowded living conditions breed disease, also sharply criticizes the government for not curbing the spread of tuberculosis through strict quarantine, and for not providing sufficient facilities and equipment for treatment. Conservatives have sarcastically dismissed the report's views as hysterical
column3: if we accept the report, we might provoke them. On the other hand, we could build a sanatorium.

column2: Fund the establishment of a local sanatorium
Ignore the report to please conservatives
Find local donors to establish a sanatorium

What's the government's latest clever move? Apparently, if the Minister of Health can be trusted, even free beds and food aren't enough for the world's homeless to beg for. It's teeth, gentlemen, a bill about teeth is on our agenda!\n\nThe ruling party is committed to passing a dental care act aimed at providing citizens with some basic dental care. But progress has been slow so far, and even some regular party members are discussing completely abandoning this idea.

The government-run "Morning Dispatch" published an article sharply condemning the decadent lifestyle of the upper elites in a certain area, calling them unpatriotic, and claiming that a small circle among these upper class people are secretly receiving aid from foreign powers to oppose the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ ruling party. This news has spread widely among the lower classes, making their tendency to violently oppose local power holders increasingly evident. Banning the newspaper's publication would be seen by the lower class as covering up our problems, which will undoubtedly anger them. However, if we don't do this, it will encourage the exposure of the upper class.

The Daily Telegraph is a newspaper widely distributed in a certain region of our country. An article published in it vividly depicted the love life of a local politician, which clearly went beyond the bounds of marriage and family. Although the article was not intended to be defamatory, it still had a great impact on the reputation of the politician who was the subject of the article. The public loves to read such tidbits, and the politician quickly became the talk of the town. The politician himself was furious about this attack on his image and has filed a lawsuit in the local court for "damaging morality and public trust," trying to ban the newspaper's publication. Stopping the newspaper will awaken local liberals, while not stopping it will increase support for publishing reform.

Having freedom of the press means dealing with some of the strangest things. "The Observer" is a strange tabloid with a considerable circulation in a certain region of our country. A commentary published in this newspaper portrayed the Foreign Minister as a secret Freemason. Although this lowbrow tabloid has always had this style, this bad article has received much more attention than usual. The public seems to somewhat believe this claim for some reason. Denying this rumor would be seen by the educated upper class as yielding to the common people, yet not denying it would cause the lower class to believe it.
But I saw him enter a small room last week...

We, the People's Committee of Free $COUNTRYNAME$, now present a simple demand to the $CAPITAL$ government: end one-party dictatorship.\n\nSimple demand, bah. Who do these thugs think they are? Leaflets with anti-government slogans have been spread throughout the bars and cafés of a certain region of our country, and we suspect they come from a local underground printing press. Local police tried to stop their distribution, and if these leaflets hadn't already spread widely in the area, they would have dealt with it as a routine matter. Undoubtedly, sealing the printing press now will cause public outrage.

A violent incident occurred today during a mayoral election in a certain province of our country. A farmer, ignoring orders, refused to fill in the government candidate's name on the ballot. This sturdy farmer was dragged out of the city hall where the election was held after breaking the noses of three local officials. He reportedly shouted on the spot about his right to vote according to his conscience and some other foolish things. We may need to punish him in some way to make an example of him. However, we must also consider the consequences of different choices.
Lock him up for three months!

Over and over again we... revise... political district boundaries to better match the people's needs for the political system. If we find that a party we don't want to see gaining electoral advantage, we only need to redraw the boundaries to let voters elect a more appropriate party. We've noticed that there are too many voices supporting liberal policies in a certain province of our country, and we're unsure whether this region should follow this trend in its elections. We could incorporate a nearby area with strong conservative support into this district, but doing so would increase local militancy.

When John Q. Public walked up to the ballot box, he instinctively knew he was being watched. The election official was watching him, a man was watching him put his ballot into the box, and an agent in the bar was watching everything through a small hole drilled in the newspaper. Somewhere, someone, somehow, was monitoring him and revealing information about his political views and voting preferences to the government. What John feared in his heart was that on some dark night someone would knock on his door and ask him to come out for tea. John Q. Public very much wished he could vote in secret.

An election fraud incident occurred in one of our regions. We have sufficient reason to believe that local conservatives won, while liberals ignored these reasons and declared themselves victorious. It is our duty to intervene at the national level to correct these frauds
column3: besides, ensuring a conservative victory will generally reduce militancy in this region. But then again... maybe it's better to let the liberals take power?

column2: Is this right? I question the government, "Is this right that a person who has worked hard all his life should be mercilessly abandoned by society just because of a trick of fate?"\n\nA farmer in a certain region of our country was disabled and disfigured in a nearly fatal threshing accident. Debates about the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ pension system have been held in the national parliament, where reformist MPs used this incident to attack the government's inaction in helping the elderly and disabled.

Along with the increase in average life expectancy in recent years, more and more families have to take care of elderly people who can no longer care for themselves. Our country's social structure is changing, while the national plans for the elderly and disabled are nowhere to be seen, and countless people have not received the attention they deserve within the system. Conservatives generally believe that the family is the primary and ultimate social organization for supporting the elderly, and the government's increasingly active intervention in this area is threatening this important social bond. On the other hand, liberals believe our pensions are severely insufficient, pointing out that many people still don't receive assistance.

In my opinion, the government's policy is not the result of malicious intent, but of stupidity. The task is still arduous.\n\nOur pension system has been attacked by the opposition within the ruling party. Apart from many administrative complaints about the system, the criticism focuses on the fact that pensions are simply too low.
I agree that some adjustments should be made in the future
I believe we must wait for the opportunity
On the contrary, we need to roll back reforms

I've worked hard enough, yet what have I got now? Exhaustion.\n\nWith the parliament's report on the pension system, the issue of pensions has been on everyone's lips and minds in the past week. The summary of the pension system in the report is quite vague, and what really caught public attention was an accompanying specific interview. The interviewee was an elderly gentleman who seemed to have been excluded from the pension system due to his low-skill work. He complained about working hard all his life, yet now having nothing but exhaustion.
I think we can make some reforms

Our tight finances have become even more difficult under the pressure of huge pensions, and at the same time the problem of systematic benefit fraud has surfaced; in some cases even thirteen-year-old children have been listed as recipients!\n\nThe Pensions and Standard of Living Committee was dissolved today without submitting its final report, and parliament began fierce debates. Obviously, internal conflicts during the hearing process caused the committee, jointly controlled by both parties, to be stalled. The resulting confusion within parliament can be used to quickly repeal some costly welfare reforms.
Get rid of these annoying things quickly

I've been marching and fighting since I was a child. I traveled north and south believing I would die, and serving the country is more glorious than anything. But now, as my life is coming to a peaceful end, I realize I have nothing to rely on.\n\nLife expectancy in $COUNTRY$ is increasing, and combined with low wages and low benefits, this means only a few people can prepare for their old age. The educated middle class hopes to see an increase in the minimum wage, while the upper class believes pensions should be raised.
I fully agree with the wealthy
I fully agree with the middle class
I don't want reform at all

As the war rages on and our country becomes increasingly war-weary, some of our ministers suggest that now might be the best time to make post-war promises to our people. Our Interior Minister has proposed and claims this idea mainly came from parliament. By promising major pension reforms after the war, we will win broad war support from the people.
Cannot make promises at this juncture
We promised the people reforms during the war. Now the war is over, and the people are expecting the government to fulfill its promises.
We can only do limited reforms
We are brewing a massive reform!
Did I really say that? Did I? Me?

I've walked all over the city looking for work, but to no avail, sir. I don't know what to do, I can't go back and wait for the grass to grow knee-high. My family believes I can support them, but what can a pauper do without work?\n\nAt the same time as job opportunities are scarce, creditors' opportunities increase, and many people from the poor strata are already living beyond their means.
They're called the poor for a reason

We want work! We need work!\n\nAccording to current economic theory, our government can only create more jobs in the industrial sector by maintaining an active economic policy. However, with unemployment exceeding five percent, some theorists within the party suggest that we should increase unemployment benefits to appease the masses before our economy recovers.
On the contrary, we need to reduce benefits
Yes, it's time to do something

This year's fiscal budget, our spending on unemployment-related items will again exceed the budget by several percentage points. That's the problem, gentlemen, percentage points. These critical percentage points are our last line of defense against bankruptcy.\n\nOur unemployment spending is beginning to exceed expectations, and some taxpayers are becoming increasingly concerned about this runaway budget situation. A committee in a certain region of our country has formed a coalition to abolish unemployment benefits, and they are striving to make national headlines.
Form a coalition supporting unemployment benefits

Workers have occupied the factory! The doors are blocked! No one can get in!\n\nWorkers in a certain region of ours have started a sit-down strike after occupying the factory. Their demands include a higher minimum wage and more unemployment benefits. We can silently support one of their goals, or choose to completely ignore the problem.

An unorganized, rampant strike has broken out in one of our regions. Workers have set up barricades at the local factory and won't let anyone in. They claim they won't stop until someone says "their demands can be met." The problem is they don't even seem to know what they want, they just keep asking for more. A union leader has offered to mediate, but the best option might be to ignore the strikers.

They call him Red John. They say he arrived with ships full of mortar and bricks, a soul full of whiskey and gunpowder. In the past few months, this roaming agitator has caused some trouble in one of our provinces. He gives speeches in the streets supporting higher wages, holds rallies in factories, and constantly talks about the need for worker solidarity. This man is clearly a troublemaker, and local police have just received word that he will be holding a meeting in a tavern tonight...

The state-run Workers' Council in one of our provinces suggests giving local workers an extra day of holiday each year as compensation for enduring hard work. In the grand scheme of things, this demand won't cost us much, but it will still be seen as overly catering to the sensitive working class, encouraging the arrogance of the mob.

So we want him removed. Not just removed, but properly removed. You know? We don't need him anymore. He's a pain, let me tell you.\n\nA union in one of our provinces is protesting factory managers' abuse of workers. This factory manager even hits workers with a cane when they happen to meet his standards of laziness. We can remove him, but the factory owner insists the manager is doing a good job.

In a certain region of ours, a group of scabs' residences have been surrounded by angry workers from the 23rd Local Workers' Union. These scabs were sent to operate the local factory to replace local strikers. The situation is tense, and factory officials have requested the military to be called in to suppress the strikers. Although violently suppressing the strikers will leave a long-term stain on our international reputation and anger the locals, not doing so would allow the socialists' apparent victory to gain them more support locally.

Painful screams interrupted the entire factory. The man's arm was severely injured by the constantly pulling machine. When the machine spat out his arm, he had fallen to the ground unconscious. His colleagues gathered around him, while the foreman repeatedly demanded workers return to work. The injured man was taken away, and the workers calmly went back to work.
Maybe it was his own problem

Despite being careful, Mr. Brown had a very difficult work week.
Monday: An inadvertent colleague and ladder nearly cost him his left eye.
Tuesday: His best shirt was ruined trying to save his arm from a bloodthirsty machine.
Wednesday: A construction worker accidentally dropped a brick from above, and he barely managed to dodge it.
Thursday: Slipped on a slick oil surface, nearly breaking his neck.
Friday: Choked on a sandwich, luckily coughed it out in time.
If there were safety rules in the factory, some of his accidents could have been completely avoided.
A brand new idea has been adopted by construction workers in $COUNTRY$: the hard hat. The first hard hats were military helmets that veterans modified for their sons
column3: this helmet saved a worker's life, and other workers began to follow suit. Sometimes even slightly modified old pots and kettles are used. This measure will improve construction safety, and fewer workers will be injured by falling objects from above.

column2: It costs too much, and workers don't always follow the rules. They ignore the safety equipment provided, and we now have more accidents than before.\n"He's lying. The safety rules are good
column3: although accidents still happen, they're far less severe than before."\n\nEmployers and workers are arguing about safety rules. Employers think safety rules are useless, too expensive, and workers don't follow them at all. But workers think accidents happen less often and they strictly follow the safety rules.

column2: Planting labor spies in our factories can prevent strikes and disperse some union power, but once workers discover our spies, they will confront us and riot. It's said that labor spies are illegal in some provinces, but they are effective and can prevent agitators from going on strike.
I wonder if this violates their personal dignity?

Two days ago, police in one of our provinces began a strike, demanding better work safety protection. The local police union is calling for complete arrest procedures and crime investigation processes, as well as improved health care plans. The government can meet these demands, but some cabinet members say the strike is illegal and threatens public security.
Who do they think they are?

Match factories have been warned that yellow phosphorus causes phosphorus necrosis of the jaw. The most obvious symptoms of phosphorus necrosis are severe toothache and swollen gums. The jaw bone will eventually rot, and removing the jaw is the only way to save the patient. Our medical experts recommend switching to expensive red phosphorus to stop this disease.
But that's not free, is it?

Few sick days, few accidents, and happy workers all mark our factory as the safest and healthiest in the world. Our health care and safety reforms are finally bearing fruit. Our workers are happy, and productivity is higher than ever.

A little boy crawled out of the chimney and sat lightly on the roof. His face and clothes were blackened by the smoke from the chimney, which shows this wasn't the first chimney he swept today. After receiving a penny tossed by the hostess, he climbed down tired from the roof.\n\nThe tragic working conditions of chimney sweeps have aroused social anger and sympathy. A committee has been established to address the poor working conditions.
We should consider legislation to end all this
Hard work is the foundation of good moral character

We must work early and late every day, work all day and all night, receive damned hourly wages according to the time clock, and have no time for anything else.\n\nThe time clock is an invention that can improve work efficiency
column3: however, labor organizations believe this invention treats workers as tools and will dampen their enthusiasm for production. We need to take a stance on this issue.

column2: If taking a break makes workers happy...
We should consider legislation to ban this vicious invention

As the living standards in $COUNTRY$ rise, more and more people from the poor strata feel they should have a greater share of the country's wealth and new prosperity. Some people involved in radical labor movements suggest enacting regulations to allow workers to have a few hours of leisure and recreation each day
column3: they even further claim this will actually increase our net output. Others don't agree with these arguments, instead claiming they violate basic economic principles and free market rules.

column2: Don't let these stupid regulations pass!
Let's try it in some places first
More free time! Less work! (This also applies to rulers, doesn't it?)

Although our labor conditions are considered the most generous in the world, the resulting lazy atmosphere is not something to be proud of. The only feasible measure is to repeal some of these reforms.\n\nParliament has been discussing maximum working hours in recent weeks. Conservatives suggest we should now adopt more business-friendly policies.
Completely wrong, we should support our unions

Three men stood on a street corner discussing life, fate, and providence. They were arrested by local police for violating the curfew and assembly ban. Local people expressed dissatisfaction, considering this an unjustified intervention by the police in citizens' lives. Regardless, this incident shows that in $COUNTRY$, government control over daily life is becoming increasingly strong.

No matter where we go, we can hear political discussions and whispers. It's becoming increasingly obvious that the people of $COUNTRY$ are gradually awakening to a more democratic tradition, so the ban on public assemblies is slowly becoming a dead letter. Just yesterday, in fact, a public assembly in a certain province of our country even had a local politician appear. When the founders of our society don't believe this law will be enforced, maybe it's time to change it.

Gentlemen, the fate of the nation is in our hands! We must strive for our rightful place in the sun, or we shall return to the old path of corruption, autocracy, and backwardness.\n\nA gentlemen's club has been established in a certain province of our country, aiming to promote the interests of its members, charity, and the country as a whole, and is expected to become a pillar of local society in the coming years.

The rally started in an orderly manner, with some people coming to Pine Street with signs. It can be clearly observed that the demonstrators on Pine Street are very dissatisfied with something, although we're not sure what exactly. Suddenly, people's emotions began to fluctuate. When some officials tried to control the situation, emotions reached a boiling point, and the assembly turned into a mob...
This is a direct result of allowing public assemblies!
This is just an unfortunate side effect of precious freedom

A group of radicals has been meeting on Cato Street for several months. The group's outspokenness about radical republicanism and attempts to recruit new members have drawn the attention of local officials. During a dawn police raid today, we confirmed our suspicions that the group was planning a coup. Although the plan was not realized, this incident triggered debates in the Upper House about whether assembly rights need to be reduced and restricted.
We must prevent the country from falling into anarchy

Due to dissatisfaction with government policies, lack of work, and social conditions, a mob of unemployed workers attacked a poorhouse. Bread and other items worth thousands in total were looted. Local officials quickly quelled the incident and arrested the ringleaders, but such incidents may continue to occur. What is the government's view on this matter?

In one of our regions, people took to the streets to express dissatisfaction with the political status quo and demand political reform. Although this was a peaceful event, conservatives and liberals still clashed. Local nobles called on the government to condemn the rally's declaration and maintain the established order. While supporting the nobles' actions will inevitably anger progressives, not doing so will also anger conservatives and nobles.
The government is willing to reform
Reform will come when the time is right

Some warm and comfortable clothes, some food, bread and cheese, a place to live. We don't want much, we don't need much, just some necessities so we can live and work in peace.\n\nA pamphlet has been published in $COUNTRY$, detailing the plight of the poor in our country. This pamphlet has attracted considerable attention, and some members of parliament have begun to speak out in support of legislation to increase the minimum wage.

Yes, we are tying ourselves in knots. Since the wage reform was implemented, nothing is more obvious than bureaucratic chaos filling civil law.\n\nSome MPs with close ties to capitalists in $COUNTRY$ have criticized the minimum wage reform, arguing it weakens the clarity and simplicity of our legal provisions. They claim the minimum wage system is unnecessary bureaucracy and can therefore be reformed. However, what they suggest is actually to abolish the minimum wage system.
I'm sure there must be a way to reach a compromise
That thick book also gives me a headache

Although I don't think I can represent all workers in $COUNTRY$, I can at least represent some of them, and they tell me we need higher wages. Prices have risen more than twice in the past few years, and we hope that capitalists aren't the only ones benefiting.\n\nA well-known labor agitator left a deep impression on several cabinet members after meeting with them. It's now widely believed in the cabinet that we should consider our minimum wage law, but there's also a faction that holds the completely opposite view.
We need to repeal some of these reforms

Minimum wage? Why would we need that? We give workers what they deserve; they can always afford housing, clothes, and food. Well, not the best housing, clothes, and food, but they get by, right?\n\nSome employers in $COUNTRY_ADJ$ are dissatisfied with our minimum wage policy, trying to abolish it, and are currently pressuring and lobbying several parliament and cabinet members.
We will maintain the current minimum wage

The proletariat has nothing to lose but its chains. It has a world to win. Workers of the world, unite!\n\nUnionism has spread like wildfire through some regions of our country. More and more agitators are coming out of factory gates, advocating worker unity against the so-called exploitation of capitalism. $COUNTRY_ADJ$ laws currently don't allow the legal formation of trade unions, but some members of our cabinet suggest that perhaps it's best to change this restriction.
Allow people to legally break the peace? Certainly not.
We should seek local support for reform.
Indeed, the time may have come to make some changes.

Additionally, since our working masses need a channel to clearly express their opinions, all employed persons across the country are obligated to join a trade union.\n\nThere's a strong voice in parliament suggesting that all employed people in $COUNTRY_ADJ$ should be obligated to join a national trade union. This proposal is supported by some in the union movement, many of whom believe it could be a good compromise for those who support further liberalization of union laws. What is the government's position?
We want to get rid of all this terrible stuff about unions
Freedom principles should guide our policy

An organization calling itself the "Mutual Aid Society" has been established in a certain province of our country. The Mutual Aid Society is a loose association of people with business connections to each other, aiming to provide economic assistance to its members through unemployment insurance, lending, and cooperative banks. The Mutual Aid Society claims it's not a trade union, but a cooperative or bank. However, some hawks in the cabinet worry that this organization is actually a front for socialist trade union activities, so they propose dissolving it.
Let the organization continue to exist

So, I was thinking me and my lads could go into the factories and talk to some people. You know, tell them about law and peace and stability and order. You know, teach them a lesson to make them see reason. After all, spare the rod and spoil the child.\n\nWe've received a petition from the employers' association, hoping we can allow them certain anti-worker practices, such as threatening to bar workers from entering the factory or directly breaking the union. Cabinet members are divided on this issue
column3: some pro-business factions not only fully agree with this idea but even suggest restricting the right to form trade unions.

column2: Give the green light to their actions
Give the red light to their actions

Slavery, this most despicable and ancient institution of tyranny and despotism, has been abolished in almost all civilized nations of the world. Yet in $COUNTRY$, our own country, this practice continues to enjoy clear legal support. A system that is clearly against nature should not be supported by law.\n\nAbolitionists have held rallies in one of our regions, supporting the liberation of slaves and the abolition of slavery.

Yes, in our country, $COUNTRY$, all people are free and equal, yet beyond our borders, slavery and serfdom still oppress the ruled in those countries.\n\nAbolitionists in $COUNTRY$ believe the government should oppose foreign slavery and support foreign abolitionist movements. However, supporting foreign dissidents obviously won't make the target country like us.
The time is not yet right
In one of our provinces, a river of protest crowds has formed on the streets
column3: it seems every man, woman, and child has put down their work to join the massive anti-government street protest. People are demanding reform of the unelected and undemocratic Upper House. Our current options are quite limited
column4: if we don't meet the mob's demands, we risk further provoking them.

column2: There has been brewing dissatisfaction with our appointed system of Upper House members among the broad masses of various classes
column3: many feel they are not well represented in parliament. Long-term agitation has begun to form a unified public opinion on this issue. Violent protests have already broken out in one region over this matter, and now the government needs to clearly define its position. Completely ignoring this issue means angering the broad masses while weakening the authority of the Upper House in their minds. Making compromises would mean strengthening liberal forces within the Upper House, which would inevitably anger conservatives.

column2: Perhaps there is room for compromise

People in a certain region feel the current Upper House representation system leaves them underrepresented. We're not sure if the dissatisfaction comes from anger about other things, but we can at least be certain they're quite unhappy. Compromising on this issue would make the whole world think we'll yield or cater to arbitrary demands, while completely ignoring it would further anger the locals. What is the government's position?
Why is this on my desk?
Perhaps equal representation would be better?

People in the densely populated regions of our country are very satisfied with the political rights and high representation they've obtained. One region in particular is especially happy because their candidate managed to secure some privileges for the local area in the past year. Although from a global perspective this doesn't deserve national attention, they're happy and that's what matters. The current question is how we should use this sudden public support. What is the government's position on this matter?
This means peace in our time

A professor from the most prestigious university in our country has published a paper on political philosophy, arguing for the use of the Jefferson method for Upper House elections. The Jefferson method is a highest-average method designed to allocate seats proportionally based on votes received by participating parties. This method can best ensure that the proportion of votes cast is close to the allocated seats. This article received both domestic and international attention upon publication. While this provides us with an opportunity to reform the electoral system, we can also simply be satisfied with the increased international prestige it brings. What is the government's position on this matter?

A national political reform club has been established in $COUNTRY$. The club has put forward an agenda to reform the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ voting system and has been able to gain considerable political support in public debates. The club wants to see the Jefferson voting system replaced by proportional representation, which they believe can more balanced and fairly represent all the people of our country. Considering the political strength the club has already gathered, it's difficult for us to directly ignore its proposals on the voting system. However, reforming the voting system is not yet on our agenda.
We should take advantage of this
The time is not yet right for reform

With the Upper House firmly in the hands of liberals, the people of our country seem to have clearly authorized us to push political reform. Now is the best time to reform our voting system, but the question is: in which direction? Since we have a clear mandate, we can more or less choose any direction. The options currently on our desk are simple plurality and the Jefferson method. Although reform still has to struggle through the legislature, this could be an excellent opportunity for us to build strength.
We don't need reform at this moment

The mob gathered outside the national legislative assembly is full of frustration and anger, and their anger is directed at us. They want charter reform, and some hotheads even hint at violent seizure of voting rights. Apart from a few radicals, the reform movement has largely remained within the scope of peaceful protest. The government has only two choices on the charter movement: support or oppose.

Our electoral system is mainly based on land ownership. A case in a certain region has drawn high attention, where a young widow lost her voting rights due to the rapid depreciation of her land value. This incident led to broader discussions about the entire property voting system, and an idea to reform the electoral system is spreading among intellectuals and progressives. The question now is how the government should respond to this current case. Should we risk angering the relatively poor residents by fixing voting standards, or allow standards to fluctuate?

Voting rights in $COUNTRY$ are directly based on wealth and property ownership. A basic principle is that only those who contribute to the public interest should be allowed to have a say in how the country should be governed. This system has had interesting effects in a certain region of our country
column3: several merchants belonging to the local middle class have earned enough money to gain a greater share of voting rights. If this becomes true, it will undoubtedly cause dissatisfaction among the local wealthy. However, depriving the middle class of their newly acquired voting rights also means a sharp increase in local militancy.

column2: Deprive them of their newly acquired voting rights

A regional council in one of our regions is holding discussions about the property-based voting system. Opponents believe the current system permanently deprives some social classes of the right to vote. We now have two choices: one is not to intervene and keep the discussion at the local level, and the other is to elevate the discussion to the national level to defend the current system.
Do not intervene and keep the discussion at the local level
Elevate the discussion to the national level

So you see, if the government actively responds to those pushing for further voting reform, it will be detrimental to the long-term peace and stability of our hometown. These noises come from other places' messy revolutionary garbage, and they are nothing but babies crying angrily.\n\nA group consisting of important capitalists, nobles, and other elites in local public life has contacted the government. The group calls itself the "Union of Concerned Citizens" and has drawn the government's attention to the existence of people who oppose further franchise reform. How should we answer them?
We'll see what we can do
Well, we certainly can't promise anything

It seems that the people in one of our provinces are getting along quite well. The political stalemate that has plagued one region of our country since the last election has finally been resolved across party lines. With a compromise reached, the local legislature can now work normally again. The locals have taken to the streets to celebrate this great victory for democracy, singing the immortal words of the poet Schiller: "Joy, thou spark from heaven, daughter of Elysium. Under thy gentle wings, all men are brothers."

I wish to donate all my wealth, whether in bonds, land, or stocks, to a foundation to further the cause of human freedom.\n\nThis is the era of laissez-faire, and the government's free trade policy has made our nation prosperous. As Adam Smith predicted, an invisible hand seems to be guiding our national destiny toward an increasingly prosperous future. For the first time in this century, we see famine becoming a thing of the past. A wealthy merchant has passed away in our country, leaving his fortune to advance the cause of free trade.
Our merchants are the pride of our nation
Our workers are the pride of our nation

Barricades have been erected on the main streets. Bakery windows have been smashed and looting has followed. The scope of food shortages is expanding across $COUNTRY$, and suppressed anger is spreading. Many blame the government's protectionist policies for these shortages, and some are even calling for the cabinet to resign. We have two choices before us: either we reshuffle the cabinet and hope to appease the public, or we wait for the storm to pass and let time prove that protectionist policies are correct.

There are almost no trade restrictions in $COUNTRY$, yet in one of our neighboring countries there are import bans on goods, especially weapons and firearms. In a border province of our country, a merchant has opened a shop to conduct cross-border arms trade. While we could inform our neighbors about the cross-border trade situation, legally we cannot do anything about this merchant—after all, free trade applies to firearms as well.
The merchant has the right to trade

A merchant in our country is in trouble because his family business has collapsed. His business is the engine of local industry, and if it falls, many locals will lose their jobs and means of livelihood. Our government's economic intervention policy allows us to help fledgling or bankrupt enterprises.

...This is the Minister for the Private Sector.\n\nOur state-owned enterprises have been plagued by inertia and corruption for quite some time. These problems have led to shortages of clothes, soap, and in some cases even food. Since even the daily needs of our people are not being met, it is only a matter of time before popular discontent erupts. It is becoming increasingly clear that we urgently need to address this situation.

The Economic Planning Bureau reported a total miscalculation in the mid-year plan, which led to an overstatement of the national reserve's military supplies. Since people in the bureau are shifting blame to each other, it is now difficult to find the source of the problem. We can compensate for our losses by cutting salaries and promoting rationalization in the administrative and bureaucratic system, but we cannot expect such actions to be popular.
Someone has to pay the price

...Therefore, every $COUNTRY_ADJ$ citizen has a solemn obligation to support the nation using all necessary and possible means in its darkest hour.\n\nAn editorial supporting the government's chauvinistic war policy has been published in a widely-circulated journal in our country. This is certainly good news. The question now is how we can use this journal to our greatest advantage.

Our military held a large-scale recruitment campaign nationwide, and volunteers came in droves. "Without strong government support for the military," the military representative said, "an operation of this scale could not have succeeded." We can use the goodwill generated by this channel to reduce national war fatigue, or we can further promote recruitment.
Our nation is tired of war
Our nation is already hungry for more

While our people struggle in unsanitary living conditions, moral degeneration, and poverty, I cannot understand why Parliament would spend millions on gunpowder and cannons. Our nation should wage a war—a war against social problems!\n\nOne of our cabinet members addressed Parliament on the government's disarmament policy. How should we use it?
People will certainly understand his meaning

The problem we are discussing now is not only a problem of our era but of all eras. Should we continue to sink deeper under the shadow of war hanging over the great powers, or should we lay down our arms and publicly declare our will for peace to the world?\n\nThe government's pacifist policy has gained support in both Parliament and among the people. We can now use this support either to reduce the militancy of the people or to continue promoting the cause of peace.

Gentlemen, God is dead, and we are about to enter a glorious new world. Behind us is a thousand years of superstition, ignorance, and darkness; before us is knowledge, science, and progress. Standing at the crossroads of history, we need to make a choice.\n\nOur government's anticlerical propaganda has, unsurprisingly, met with opposition from $COUNTRY_ADJ$ clergy.

It has become increasingly clear to observers over the past few years that the combination of Church and state cannot endure indefinitely, given more conflicts between them. The current conflict—well, since I have no better word for it—can only be described as a domestic violence incident.\n\nThe ruling party's secularization policy has brought a minor crisis to one region. A charitable foundation established by clergy in that region received government support. Additionally, religious organizations were permitted to rent public buildings at rents well below market value.

We are different, all of us living in $COUNTRY$, speaking or singing in different voices, yet we have one thing in common. We are all $COUNTRY$ people.\n\nOld conflicts are subsiding, and former enemies are now standing arm in arm. This sounds like a fairy tale, but our ruling party's pluralist policy has ushered in an era of understanding and tolerance for our nation. The calm may be deceptive, but it is still calm.
We should seek common ground while reserving differences!
All men are brothers under heaven!

Our society today is in a moral decline. What we urgently need is to launch a moral revival movement across the land of $COUNTRY$. We must reclaim ancient values, return to the foundations upon which our nation was built, and let the things that once made our nation great shine forth again.\n\nA preacher in one region of our country has established a small but locally influential organization, claiming its purpose is to promote a moral revival movement in $COUNTRY$. There is no doubt that this organization can echo the ruling party's moralistic policies, so we might consider it an important ally.

But today our high-quality products are being flooded by cheap foreign low-quality products, so it is extremely important to protect the local market from the destructive influence of foreign competition.\n\nIndustries across our nation have faced foreign competition in recent years. In response, local protectionist lobbies advocate subsidizing important national industries and restricting imports.

In these days, when the ghost of mercantilism has returned, those who do not want to see borders closed and barriers erected between peoples of the world must stand up. They must make their voices heard in the court of public opinion.\n\nWith the formation of an organization called the "Free Trade and Repeal League" in one region of our country, the flames of public debate burn brighter. The organization is dedicated to opposing the government's protectionist policies and repealing some of the core laws behind those policies.
Protectionist policies will not be shaken

So, in this case, economic freedom must be discussed separately from larger issues of public morality. The free trade of goods means a continuous flow of foreign obscenity, degradation, and immorality, and this must be changed.\n\nMoralists and free traders in one region of our country have engaged in debate. Moralists want us to ban certain international trade and business activities that threaten public morality.

Therefore, the struggle of our motherland is also our struggle. For the motherland's cause is not only just, it also has a solid moral foundation.\n\nOur government's policy of supporting public morality has borne fruit, and now moralist circles lend their full support to the war. Some insiders have even begun to describe the struggle of $COUNTRY$ as a moral crusade.
Brave warriors, you may rest for now!

Considering the current social instability, I think we should temporarily restrict the right of the public to gather in public places. The instability in the cities is all caused by mobs, and when we deal with the mobs, order will naturally be restored to the cities.\n\nIn light of continuing social instability in $COUNTRY$, a conservative faction in the upper house has begun pushing for a temporary ban on public gatherings. Other parties have opposed the ban, fearing that this temporary measure might eventually become institutionalized.
A temporary ban will help restore order

I just want some bread, I've been standing here for four hours. I don't think they have any bread at all.\n\nBread queues snake from one block to another. Due to inefficient transportation and logistics, there have been persistent food supply problems in one of our provinces. Locals want the central government to take measures to solve the bread problem.

$COUNTRY$ was once a respected member of the international community, but over the years our voice has been getting smaller and our opinions have been ignored. I think now we must re-establish our rightful place internationally. Some may think I am advocating adventurism, but without taking risks we would never have achieved what we have today as a nation.\n\nThe Politburo held a meeting to discuss our international situation, where some hawkish members advocated launching a foreign war to divert domestic tensions and strengthen our international position.

We will not accept the evil imperialist propaganda instigated by capitalists and arms dealers, who delude the workers of one country to fight against the workers of another! Workers of the world are brothers, we all speak the same language, we share the same sweat. Wars make capitalists rich, but it is our workers who bleed!\n\nDangerous elements within the trade union movement organized a strike in one of our provinces. Although this strike was conducted in the name of peace and solidarity, some in our cabinet suspect that the underlying purpose of this demonstration was to demonstrate the power of socialism.
We need greater support for the war
Tonight we'll go to hell for dinner

We were surprised we got so many votes when our headquarters was closed, officials couldn't work normally, and our campaign was harassed. This policy of open political harassment is a stain on our nation's conscience, both for our nation and for the voters... if I may point out... since no election in $COUNTRY$ is truly democratic, it is an insult to them.\n\nA prominent liberal politician from one region of our country spoke out fiercely against the harassment policies in our election system and demanded a government response.
Our government has no plans to push political reform yet
The government agrees to gradually push through some limited reforms

The censorship department has found itself overwhelmed with work in recent years. The department's executive director has complained on several occasions that his subordinates cannot cope with the growth in materials to be reviewed. The other day, a newspaper published an article attacking government policy, which included personal defamation of several cabinet members, exposing the fact that the overloaded censorship department has almost reached its breaking point. When questioned about how this article passed censorship, the department pointed out that they had already reported insufficient resources. However, several cabinet members claimed the department had sufficient resources, and the problem was basic organizational management.

Gentlemen, here are the consequences of the ridiculous speculative behavior of our industrial magnates! Hundreds of thousands, even millions of dollars have been squandered on high-risk investments, speculative real estate, and bonds. If we look further, these funds have played no practical value beyond boasting. I call on this assembly to intervene and correct these outstanding issues, and to do so the government must pursue strong policies, establish regulations, and strengthen government intervention.\n\nA member of parliament condemned our government's economic policies by listing a series of failed investments in the private sector.
If the problem persists, then regulate it
Economic freedom and human progress are closely related

People should know what they think. Publishing such an article in a country like $COUNTRY$? Anyway, it's happened. A widely-read daily newspaper published a blasphemous article harshly criticizing all things religious. The article's author came from a somewhat well-known intellectual circle, and its publication may signal that we are entering an age of irreligion. Moralists demand that the newspaper retract the article and issue a formal apology to the offended religious institutions. However, several reform-minded elites believe the author has the right to exercise his freedom of speech. After all, the press in $COUNTRY$ is free, so that's one reason.
It seems we've given our people too much freedom
The author acted within his legal rights
Where Does the Nile Come From?
The Royal Geographical Society has announced a reward for the first explorer to discover the source of the Nile.
We will not participate in this foolish display.
Our national expedition did not succeed in finding the source of the Nile, but they hope the next expedition will succeed.
There is no need for this pointless activity.
The second expedition to find the source of the Nile has mysteriously disappeared, and we can only assume we have lost them. Shall we make a third attempt?
Our brave explorers have reached the source of the Nile and brought glory and prestige to our great motherland!
This is a glorious day for our nation's science!
The Royal Geographical Society has announced a reward for the first expedition to reach the North Pole.
There's nothing to explore at the North Pole but ice.
Our national expedition did not succeed in reaching the North Pole, but they hope the next expedition will succeed.
The second expedition to reach the North Pole has mysteriously disappeared, and we can only assume we have lost them. Shall we make a third attempt?
First to Reach the North Pole!
Our brave explorers have raised the flag at the North Pole for the first time, bringing glory and prestige to our great motherland!
The Royal Geographical Society has announced a reward for the first expedition to reach the South Pole.
Our national expedition did not succeed in reaching the South Pole, but they hope the next expedition will succeed.
The second expedition to reach the South Pole has mysteriously disappeared, and we can only assume we have lost them. Shall we make a third attempt?
First to Reach the South Pole!
Our brave explorers have raised the flag at the South Pole for the first time, bringing glory and prestige to our great motherland!

A French nobleman named Pierre de Coubertin, inspired by new interest in ancient Greek civilization and the idea of sports as an important part of social development, proposed reviving the Olympic Games and believed they could serve as a friendly platform for international competition to promote peace. Should our nation join the International Olympic Committee to organize the first games?
Our Nation to Host the First Olympics?
Since the Olympic tradition originates from our sacred land, the International Olympic Committee has invited our government to host the first modern Olympic Games. Should we accept this proposal?
Yes, this is a great opportunity to showcase our progress.
No, our limited resources should be put to better use.
Although the Olympic Games originated in Greece, the International Olympic Committee has decided to let our nation host the first modern Olympic Games. Should we accept the proposal?
With the host nation determined, the International Olympic Committee has sent invitations to its member nations to participate in the competition. Will we participate?
Athletes from around the world have gathered in our capital city to compete in the Olympic Games. This is a great moment for our nation to showcase itself on the world stage.
We declare the first modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our athletes have won in the recent Olympic competitions and returned home with gold, silver, and bronze medals.
This is the glory of our nation's youth!
Our Nation to Host the Second Olympics?
The International Olympic Committee has invited our nation to host the next Olympic Games. Should we accept the invitation?
We declare the second modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Third Olympics?
We declare the third modern Olympic Games officially open.
We declare the third modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Fourth Olympics?
We declare the fourth modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Fifth Olympics?
We declare the fifth modern Olympic Games officially open.
We declare the fifth modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Sixth Olympics?
We declare the sixth modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Seventh Olympics?
We declare the seventh modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Eighth Olympics?
We declare the eighth modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Ninth Olympics?
We declare the ninth modern Olympic Games officially open.
Our Nation to Host the Tenth Olympics?
We declare the tenth modern Olympic Games officially open.

The late Swedish inventor and industrialist Alfred Nobel's will established a foundation with his entire life's wealth. This foundation will award prizes annually to researchers who have made outstanding contributions in various fields. These fields include chemistry, physics, or medicine, as well as writers who have created pioneering literature and activists who have greatly promoted international peace and cooperation.
This is a great act by a great Swede
A distinguished scientist from our nation has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physics.
This is a great honor for our nation's physics research.
A distinguished scientist from our nation has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Chemistry
This is a great honor for our nation's chemistry research.
Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
A distinguished scientist from our nation has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
This is a great honor for our nation's medical research.
A distinguished writer from our nation has been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Literature.
This is a great honor for our nation's literary tradition.
An activist from our nation has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for outstanding contributions to global peace and cooperation.
This is a great honor for our nation and the global cause of peace.
Our Nation to Host a World's Fair?

A delegation representing the major business and commercial interests of our nation has proposed hosting a World's Fair in our capital. Holding such an event would provide us with an excellent opportunity to showcase our economic capabilities and technological expertise to the world, and could greatly promote exports by promoting our goods on the world stage. Should we support this idea?
An excellent idea! We support it.
Our resources would be better used elsewhere.

People from around the world have come to our capital to attend the World's Fair. National pavilions compete for attention, and an endless array of buildings and marvels highlight the extraordinary strength of our economy and culture to visitors.
Our Nation to Host a Regional Trade Fair?

A delegation representing the major business and commercial interests of our nation has proposed hosting a Regional Trade Fair in our capital. Holding such an event would provide us with an excellent opportunity to showcase our economic capabilities and technological expertise to our neighbors, and could greatly promote exports and good neighborly relations by promoting our goods. Should we support this idea?

People from neighboring nations have come to our capital to attend the World's Fair. National pavilions compete for attention, and an endless array of buildings and marvels highlight the extraordinary strength of our economy and culture to visitors.
Our Nation to Host a Colonial Exhibition?

A delegation representing the major business and commercial interests of our empire has proposed hosting a Colonial Exhibition in our capital. Holding such an event would provide us with an excellent opportunity to showcase the economic and cultural wealth of our colonies, and could greatly promote exports and strengthen domestic support for the empire by promoting our imperial goods. Should we support this idea?

People from the empire and around the world have come to our capital to attend the Colonial Exhibition. Colonial pavilions compete for attention, and an endless array of buildings and marvels highlight the importance of our economic and cultural mission to visitors from home and abroad.
A magnificent display of our empire's power and wealth!
A revolutionary wind blows, and storms appear on the horizon. Enthusiastic liberalism sweeps across $COUNTRYNAME$.
You don't need to know which way the wind blows.

The potato late blight fungus, a terrible potato blight, has struck $PROVINCENAME$. Farmers starving in some areas have already dragged their families and left their hometowns, and this disease has led to the spread of famine threats in the region.
This spring, crops in $PROVINCENAME$ are growing well. The potato blight in $PROVINCENAME$ has finally subsided.
A pamphlet condemning the state of our nation has triggered a demonstration in one region, and this situation shows signs of spreading nationwide.

A new newspaper has begun publication in $PROVINCENAME$. This newspaper, called the "$PROVINCENAME$ Pioneer Herald," publishes sharp political, literary criticism, and local news, and quickly became the mouthpiece of local liberal politics.
I hope there's no obituary for me.
A branch of the Chartist Association has been established in $PROVINCENAME$, calling for expanded voting rights and the abolition of the current property-restricted voting system.

A wave of liberal thought has begun to spread in $PROVINCENAME$. While not certain, there are signs that a recent secret society movement seems to be somewhat related to it. Whether it's the "Rosicrucians" or the "Freemasons" or the Bavarian "Illuminati," someone is leading and spreading this thought in $PROVINCENAME$.
...Maybe they just want us to think that way?

Smoke from factory chimneys dissipates into the sky dyed red by scattered sparks. Deep in the city, amid the rumble and smoke of industrialization, countless workers crave better conditions and pay. The Luddites in $PROVINCENAME$ have taken to the streets with fury.

Immorality seeps through every crevice of legal authority like water. Liberals in $PROVINCENAME$, banned from public assembly, have resorted to holding secret political gatherings under the guise of banquets and parties.

Like rats carrying disease, modernization advocates scurry across our national borders. The liberal wave has spread from the neighboring province to $PROVINCENAME$. We should dispatch some troops to control the situation.
We need to think of something

When revolutionary armies threaten to challenge the traditional order of Europe, opposing them becomes our sacred mission. The Jacobins are a collective of unredeemable blowhards and mercenary merchants. Look what Robespierre brought to France—their radicalism is being imposed on $COUNTRY$.\n\nThe widespread liberal wave in $COUNTRY$ has sparked a strong backlash, and a leading conservative intellectual has written an anti-Jacobin pamphlet.

Let's be clear, those who talk about revolutionary causes are opposing the cause and arrangement of our Almighty God.
