This verdict was seen as a milestone victory in the American abolitionist movement, and public attention to the slavery issue reached new heights.

Yesterday earlier we received a request from the $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ Congress, applying to become a state of the United States of America. At the same time, a state constitution along with a state boundary map was submitted to us. The vast majority of the public wants us to accept $FROMCOUNTRY$ as a member of our great and glorious republic.
Trust the public, make the right choice!
We have broken the "Anaconda Plan" blockade, and now our coastline is navigable again. What exhilarating news!

As the number of new immigrants in the Black Hills region increases, conflicts between immigrants and the local Sioux have also escalated. We received news from the local area that an Indian named "Sitting Bull" is leading an armed organization called the "War Party" that is rapidly rising in the Dakota Territory.
We will drive these Sioux from their lands!

Sitting Bull and the warriors he led surrendered, and the Sioux lost this war. Perhaps we will go to war with other Indian nations in the future, but the Sioux have been conquered. They will never again be allowed to have a threatening armed force, and the Sioux have had no future since the moment they went to war with us. We feel a bit sad: this once-great tribe has become a memory in textbooks because of us.

A person named Victorio led a group of Apaches from New Mexico to rise up, and several colonists have been brutally killed. Because white people continuously invaded territories considered part of the Apache homeland, Victorio and his followers were resentful and determined to resist the authority of the United States.
They will yield, sooner or later.

Geronimo, the respected leader of the Apache tribe, and a small group of his supporters surrendered to the army led by Colonel Henry Lawton. With the capture of Geronimo, the last resistance force of the Apache in the western region was also eliminated, and this once-proud Indian tribe fell into silence. Many years later, on his deathbed, Geronimo told his nephew that the decision he regretted most in his life was surrendering to the white man.

...We will no longer endure the injustices we have suffered, we will never retreat, we will no longer be silent! Give women the right to vote!\n\nThe growing liberal and feminist movements in recent years have driven women in $COUNTRY$ to establish feminist organizations, demanding that the government grant women equal legal rights with men. Women across $COUNTRY$ have left the roles considered their due: housewives or unpaid nannies, and instead demanded the right to vote, the right to work, and even the right to own their own property.
We cannot allow feminists to run rampant at this critical juncture
As long as they have broad support, we won't oppose it...

A small group of women organized an international conference on women's rights. The two-day conference in $CAPITAL$ invited not only women representatives but also a considerable number of men. However, on the first day, only women representatives were allowed to participate in the discussions. On the second day, women representatives used this political strategy to pass a series of proposals. Despite the differences between men and women representatives not being resolved, the conference decided to pass ten reform proposals, demanding that women have equal rights with men in the following matters: family law, education rights, property rights, work rights, religious freedom, etc.
Use the secret police to arrest these dangerous revolutionaries
Congratulate the conference and express support for their cause

During the World Anti-Slavery Convention, some women representatives were also representatives of the Women's Rights Convention. Before the conference officially began, male representatives voted to not allow women to participate in the conference or to require women representatives to sit in a designated area far from the sight of men. Another group of male representatives opposed excluding women from the conference and decided that if their opinion was not adopted, they would choose to sit in the area adjacent to the women representatives.
No, never let them attend the conference!
Give them the right to attend.
Women Start Working in Social Work

When war broke out and all able-bodied adult men were conscripted into the military, many women began leaving their homes to engage in social work. However, when they realized their salaries were only half of men's, women began to demand equal pay for equal work.

The rumors that feminists are holding a conference to seek women's political rights are not unfounded. The two-day conference invited both male and female representatives. Representatives discussed whether to seek women's suffrage, but no consensus was reached. Finally, representatives made ten reform proposals, including: demanding that women achieve equal status in the family, the right to education, the right to work, religious freedom, etc.

$CAPITAL$'s bad weather is always working against us, and the mud everywhere is the best portrayal of the bad weather. However, more troubling is the "Mud March." This march for women's suffrage attracted more than 3000 women from different organizations such as the Textile Workers' Association, the Temperance Association, the Artists' Association, etc.

A newspaper from a neighboring region declared: Despite the very bad weather, quite a lot of people joined the "Mud March." "...A few red and white tones outlined an exciting rose emblem, surrounded by red and white handkerchiefs for publicity, with the specific content using white banners and bright red letters: Ladies (demand your right to vote)!"
National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies and National Women's Social and Political Union

These two groups call themselves the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies and the National Women's Social and Political Union respectively. Both groups fought for women's suffrage. However, the latter put forward more radical demands such as: wanting simpler divorce procedures, eliminating discrimination against women in employment and salary, etc.
Support the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies!
Support the National Women's Social and Political Union!
Campaign for the "Married Women's Property Act"

Married women not only cannot enjoy independent property rights, but their legal personality is also attached to their husbands. Married women have become people completely unprotected by law. We want to change all this, we demand that women be able to dispose of their own property according to their own wishes. We demand that the court regard wives and husbands as two independent legal personalities.\n\nDisadvantaged women have awakened once again.
Sign the Married Women's Property Act

Thank you so much for your support! "Without your support, we would never have been able to reach this point."

"Hmph, they are always so insatiable." "I'll make them end this in tears"

Some dissatisfied people expressed their resentment against the "Married Women's Property Act." Most views, however, held that passing "Married Women's Property Rights" was a good thing.
National Women's Social and Political Union: Women Should Be Educated

If Professor, you don't want to see a female student wearing a Scottish cap appear, then I can remove my headdress and sit in the corner of the classroom, but I won't skip class because of that.\n\nThe female student looked directly into the professor's eyes until he changed his mind and sat down. She was the first female student to step into the university campus, and obviously most students could not accept women appearing on campus. When she first applied for admission to this university, the teacher put the question of whether to allow her admission to a student vote, and the participating students even thought it was a farce. Now she has learned to endure all kinds of discrimination and rudeness. More women are choosing to pressure the government to gain the right to enter university.
National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies: Women Should Be Educated

If Professor, you don't want to see a female student wearing a Scottish cap appear, then I can remove my headdress and sit in the corner of the classroom, but I won't skip class because of that.\n\nThe female student looked directly into the professor's eyes until he changed his mind and sat down. She was the first female student to step into the university campus, and obviously most students could not accept women appearing on campus. When she first applied for admission to this university, the teacher put the question of whether to allow her admission to a student vote, and the participating students even thought it was a farce. Now she has learned to endure all kinds of discrimination and rudeness. More women are choosing to pressure the government to gain the right to enter university.
Pressure on the Senate to vote on women's political rights is increasing day by day. The National Women's Social and Political Union is petitioning and demonstrating almost daily.
We will hold detailed discussions on this issue.
We will not allow this to happen.

Breaking glass, attempting to burn buildings, attacking officers... Although the attacked officer was not seriously injured, I can be sure these are enough to make them lose face. "What made you do such things?" the police asked.
The female suspect refused to answer any of his questions. The officer had no choice but to leave the prison, but he was soon stopped by another officer.
"Since her arrest, this female suspect has started a hunger strike. What should we do?".
"Best not to do anything at this stage, just provide her with enough food and water, don't force her to eat, she will eat when she's hungry."

It's been two days, she still won't eat or drink. I really can't understand why she's doing this? She is a member of the women's suffrage movement, and perhaps she wants to gain more support through a hunger strike. "What should we do?"

'Quick, come quick, that women's suffrage movement member, she, she's dead!' The hunger strike and the forced feeding action taken by the police killed her. The growing public dissatisfaction with the police's forced feeding action forced the government to quickly submit the Cat and Mouse Act to parliament. The act required that physically weak prisoners be released on medical parole and re-imprisoned after their health recovered.

The Cat and Mouse Act released many members of the women's suffrage movement, and they were planning how not to be thrown back into prison after their health recovered. So other members and leaders of the organization created a protection group of thirty women calling themselves the "Special Guard." Members of the Special Guard have all undergone strict karate training. Their training locations are chosen in hidden places to avoid police attention. Shortly after the establishment of the Special Guard, a fistfight broke out with police trying to arrest leaders of the women's suffrage movement. This fistfight attracted widespread media attention and made the discussion of women's suffrage in the House of Lords reach an unprecedented depth.
We must take measures to ease the situation.
We must never allow this to happen!

The long and arduous struggle of women has finally borne fruit. The leaders of the women's suffrage movement submitted their political demands to the Speaker of the House of Lords, who turned their request into a bill on political reform and submitted it to parliament for voting. Now, you will cast the decisive vote on the bill, and your vote will give all issues a clear answer: will women be legally equal to men and gain the same rights as men?

Workers from different industries and places have formed a labor union, which will negotiate with you on wage levels, work regulations, complaint procedures, reward and punishment regulations, welfare benefits, safety protection, and labor relations.

'We need bread, but we also need roses!' Women surrounded the factory, shouting slogans and holding signs that read 'We need bread, but we also need roses!' The factory work was extremely hard and workers always faced various dangers. After implementing the eight-hour workday, the capitalists began cutting workers' wages and laid off half of the employees. As a result, the remaining half of the employees had to face double the work and only half the salary. Before long, workers began to rise up against the capitalists.

Factory or slaughterhouse? "Slaughterhouse" is becoming the nickname for the factory, and almost every day workers are killed in various accidents, most of which are caused by cranes. Decreasing safety standards and increasingly low wages triggered a major strike that resulted in more than twenty deaths and injuries. When workers realized their wages were being deducted, they demanded a reasonable explanation from factory managers, but management refused this request. Finally, angry workers chose to strike. Management chose to hire strikebreakers and private bodyguards to protect themselves. When the strikebreakers arrived at the factory, they were greeted with stones and clubs. After the police arrived, bloody clashes broke out with workers and strikebreakers, directly causing more than twenty deaths.
'Eight hours for work, eight hours for recreation, eight hours for rest' 'We want bread, we want roses too!' Slogans echoing from neighboring provinces have finally reached us.

'The chemicals used in the factory make us sick' 'Just being in the factory is absolutely harmful to health, let alone working there!' Workers demand higher wages and better working conditions, which factory owners don't want to see. Just fifty gold coins can rebuild part of the factory buildings and improve the working environment.
People marched in the streets supporting various labor organizations. It was a calm and glorious day.

More, more! More general strikes in $CAPITAL$. Workers demand higher wages. More, more! More...\n\nA socialist newspaper called Forward! was founded in $CAPITAL$. The newspaper reported on various strikes, current affairs, and socialist movements at home and abroad.
Aren't they saying there's no left-leaning media...

Despite continuous criticism, a multi-party committee was established to create a national employment training institute to help the unemployed.\nThe first national employment training institute officially began work after the committee's first meeting, and about a thousand unemployed people found jobs through it. Other unemployed people were not so fortunate and could only return home tired and hungry. All workers who did not find jobs were promised free bread, but this soon turned into handing out money instead. This was a huge mistake.
This is really not a good sign.

Workers and sympathizers took to the streets to protest. The closure of the national employment training institute and the layoffs of many workers triggered strong protests from a large number of workers. When the government took measures, the workers fought back: they occupied some buildings and set up barricades. The number of resisters is increasing every day

Workers from several different factories have formed a trade union confederation, through which they will negotiate on salaries, work regulations, complaint handling procedures, reward and punishment mechanisms, welfare benefits, factory safety measures, etc.
To achieve self-sufficiency and begin exporting from $PROVINCENAME$, we should establish new agricultural settlements.
A small private army calling itself the Black Shirts, led by the obscure Ben-Mussor, launched a random attack on our troops. The attack resulted in the deaths of several soldiers.
The Black Shirts led by Ben-Mussor are marching on $CAPITAL$.
A group of soldiers calling themselves the "Free Corps" has also risen up against the government, influenced by the Black Shirts in the neighboring province. This is somewhat of a threat.
This is not a threat to us.

An excerpt from the newspaper "I Am Everywhere":

"...Our country should expand its armaments and strike first for national interests. The military should be used to..." "...Guarantee national unity, conquer territories that have belonged to our country since ancient times..." "...Children are our future..."

The newspaper enthusiastically promotes chauvinism, fascism, and Zionism.
After causing widespread destruction locally, the Black Shirts attacked a group of moderate socialists and liberals. The Black Shirts captured them and took them to Central Park for execution.
The Free Corps, determined to take action, attacked a group of moderate socialists and liberals. The Free Corps captured them and took them to Central Park for execution. They went too far.

No one should go hungry or freeze. A food distribution point at the street corner caught your attention. Healthy hot meals are distributed to hungry unemployed people, along with a pamphlet full of fascist propaganda.

The beer hall was filled with the clinking of glasses and the singing of drunkards until the door was forcibly broken down by a group of Black Shirts.

"There are six hundred people in the hall. No one is allowed to leave!"

An uninvited guest jumped onto a table and began to rhapsodize about revolution, national unity, and forming a new government. Some guests were moved by him and roared their desire to join the revolution.

...Moreover, under the people's strong demands for reform and social justice, the riots caused by famine, and class struggle, has our party supported the cause of $COUNTRY_ADJ$ workers? No, nothing except continuous empty promises that would eventually be fulfilled! Colleagues, for these and more reasons, as a member here, I can no longer accept myself as a liberal, unless we restore the original meaning of this word: being a socialist.\n\nA radical faction in the House of Lords defected to socialism, advocating social reform, equality, and worker solidarity. We can pressure the party organization to maintain internal cohesion.

Social democracy has only nominal democracy. While this party desperately tries to maintain the facade, for any honest observer there is ample evidence that it has long since departed from parliamentary order and transferred power to antiquated mass movements, rigid dogmas, and cronyism. When the embankment breaks, let the people know that some are swimming against the tide.\n\nA group of malcontents in the House of Lords has allied against the socialists who refuse to pass political reform. By applying political pressure, we can influence the composition of this new opposition.
House of Lords Charter Reform Debate

...Moreover, we self-proclaimed conservatives say that the lower classes are unfit for representation due to deficiencies in education and moral and social understanding. I now say to the conference that this statement is nothing more than a basic confusion of the chicken-and-egg problem. Because if it were not for the long-standing deliberate design by this aristocratic assembly representing the lower classes, perhaps those deficiencies would not have been left unattended until they festered.\n\nAn impassioned speech in the House of Lords today led several people to defect to the liberal faction supporting charter reform. Public demands for universal suffrage continue to grow.
A Meeting on the Assembly Issue

...You see, my dear old friend, I need your support in the House of Lords to pass this motion.\n\nThe liberal faction in the House of Lords has launched a striking offensive against the "swing voters" of other parties. They are gathering support in the House of Lords to abolish the ban on public assemblies. The vote campaign has achieved some success, and we need to decide how to respond.

...I saw red flags on the streets of $CAPITAL$, and I believe the only way to fight this rising socialist tide is through reconciliation.\n\nA group of reform-minded liberals in the House of Lords decided to stand with the socialists on the issue of trade union reform. The group claims our current policy is too intolerant of public opinion swings, and they argue that labor reform is necessary to protect worker interests. They are forming a parliamentary bloc. Should we manipulate parliament behind the scenes to counter this action?

...It is now, with the new forces, that I reiterate the difficult problem to which I have yet to get any response from this House: what to do about the press reform issue? I, and many colleagues with me, have always maintained that the time for reform is now, but this conference is still completely unwilling to give even an answer, let alone a policy.\n\nReform-minded members of parliament have reorganized into a new alliance to advance the press reform agenda. Capitalizing on widespread public support for freedom of speech, liberals in the House of Lords are gaining strength.

This is why we can only answer 'no' to further reform proposals! We came here with a limited reform agenda, but the reform discussion we are now hearing threatens to overturn every sacred and ancient existing institution in this land, and ultimately disintegrate the basic structure of our society.\n\nDissatisfied with the prevailing political winds, an unholy alliance of several factions in the House of Lords has formed into a bloc dedicated to opposing all further efforts to fundamentally reform the political system.
The party whip will bring them into line

...Any objections?\n\nAt an hastily convened extraordinary meeting of the House of Lords, a strange constitutional reform motion was passed. The proposed system allows political parties to appoint members of the House of Lords. From all aspects of this action, it is clear that this is a premeditated coup by the ruling reactionary party.
Question the legality of the motion

The House of Lords held a debate on the issue of wage slavery, and socialists are gaining strong support by advocating the necessity of wage reform. Widespread public support for further social reform has led several nominally non-socialist members of the House to come under increasing pressure from their constituencies, causing some of them to consider defecting to the socialist bloc. Through political maneuvering, we may be able to prevent a large-scale defection of members to socialism, but this may be seen as a dictatorial act by broad segments of our population.

The liberal core collectively pushes for pressure on the political reform agenda. The liberals expressed their concerns about the following facts: the intrusion of state institutions into citizens' private lives, and the political system being firmly controlled by a few at the expense of the majority. They threatened to block all bills in the House of Lords until these concerning facts are addressed. Members of several other parties are considering aligning with the liberals on the political reform issue, and any hesitation on our part is likely to exacerbate public dissatisfaction with the slow pace of reform.

...Therefore, it seems to me that there is a flaw in our widely praised system, namely that the lowest-level workers cannot even afford the most basic sanitary living conditions for themselves and their families. Dirty sheds filled with smoke sprang up like mushrooms in the shadows of accumulated smoke, crowded together, they are the damp and dark breeding grounds for cholera, tuberculosis, and moral decay. My colleagues, a limited sanitary reform would greatly help improve these problems.\n\nThe House of Lords is in chaos due to its apparent inability to promote the social reforms that society urgently needs.
Postpone the issue until the next election

I believe an agreement can be reached.\n\nA temporary majority in the House of Lords has formed on the issue of unemployment benefits. Speaking in parliament, the conservative group leader believed that these measures alone could be passed as an experiment in national policy. Given the public's dissatisfaction with the plight of today's unemployed, his group will support a proposal on moderate unemployment assistance. Although the liberals are still not satisfied with the proposal, not passing it would be seen as missing an opportunity for reform.

I believe the only natural solution to the current dispute is to advocate that my conservative colleagues take the lead on this issue.\n\nA certain conservative national policy, coupled with rising combativeness, has received strong public support. This has caused friction within the House of Lords. Several liberal members are considering defecting to the conservative side, and only by generously using the party whip can the liberals be kept in their seats.

Recently, a red tornado seems to have completed a masterpiece in the House of Lords, with more and more members expressing willingness to cooperate with and support the ruling socialists. If we don't want to see the socialists gain a single majority in the House, now is the time to act.

The rifle party is showing off both on the streets and in the House of Lords. Several conservative members are desperately considering defecting to the fascist side, and blocking the reorganization will undoubtedly increase the combativeness of the fascists.

The small liberal party is using the social unrest in $COUNTRYNAME$ to achieve political goals, trying to win over some more left-leaning conservatives in the House of Lords to their cause. The current topic of discussion is election reform, and some conservatives are considering supporting the liberal party on this issue.

I believe, therefore, that this freedom should not be lost in this country, and she needs us to maintain constant vigilance for it.\n\nA liberal member of the House of Lords delivered an inspiring speech in parliament, criticizing the government's inability to improve the country's social unrest trend. How should the government respond?

A socialist agitator in the House of Lords delivered a lengthy speech against the government from the rostrum, mocking the government's inability to quell the growing social unrest in $COUNTRYNAME$. He claimed that under socialism, the state, the party, and the people would speak with one voice.
Maybe there is something for us to learn

This ancestral law is so perfect that it was established long ago, passing through the entire century, through countless eras until today. A conservative member of the House of Lords highly praised the glory of our country in a parliamentary speech, putting us on a pedestal.
Today, a reactionary member of the House of Lords gave a lengthy speech in parliament, declaring that we must reclaim the land that has been ours since ancient times.

Our merchants have the right to freely traverse the seas and lands, and no government can interfere with this right.\n\nA young member of the House of Lords has recently shone brightly. He belongs to the anarchist faction and has recently been vigorously inciting people to support free trade, and the people seem to be listening to him. We can take this opportunity to push the laissez-faire agenda, or ignore his speech, but this will also anger his supporters.

Today, in cities across $COUNTRYNAME$, the forces of law and order marched down the avenues in neat uniforms, showing their presence to everyone. In this era of fanaticism, each of them will unremittingly maintain order and stability. The police agency needs to formulate a long-term policy for their work. How can we make full use of this event?

Our territory may be broken, but our army will not! When their ranks march past, we see in their eyes only dedication to $COUNTRYNAME$ and the lofty ideals our country relies on. These people are worthy of the name of soldiers
column3: they have cultivated strong characters and firm belief in their motherland since childhood, and they will fight to defend their homeland. Long live $COUNTRYNAME$!

column2: With dreams of bleeding and fighting in the great war, young soldiers set out from the barracks. On their way in close formation, they received unanimous respect from women and children of all ages. People standing by the roadside and at the train station saw them off with kisses and smiles, and decorated the soldiers' weapons with flowers.

In our factories and workshops, $COUNTRY_ADJ$ freemen make new discoveries and progress every day. The progress of science and technology is closely related to the free exchange of ideas, and there is no place easier for this than $COUNTRY$. Our freedom makes our country a powerhouse of scientific and technological progress.
Let other countries sing our praises!

Although some of our past policies were seen as territorial expansion, now even foreigners believe we are only further advancing our national cause of liberty. Friendly organizations abroad have sent congratulatory messages warmly celebrating our recent victories. Where is the future direction of our nation?

As unrest spreads through $COUNTRY$, demonstrators flood the streets of $CAPITAL$ to protest government policies and call for political and economic reform. By deploying more police forces to control the situation, we can prevent further escalation of violence. But at the same time, it has always been our country's policy that the masses have the right to speak their minds. By reaffirming our traditional values, we will appear stronger in the eyes of other nations.

Just now, they marched and chanted, and desperate angry voices echoed through the streets. Now, as anger turns to calm and conflict to peace, the scene returns to quiet. No matter how much we elaborate on our country's ailments, it's all just salt rubbed into old wounds. After all, our people work equally and share weal and woe together, and they know this well.

They sweat, they toil, they keep moving forward, driving up our country's pride and prestige. The men and women of our country come from a nation of excellent stock and feel they are part of a common group, sharing the same fate, which makes them feel that their extra efforts will always be rewarded. The value of equality has made our people invest more effort this year. How should we take advantage of this?

End the war! Give bread to the workers of $CAPITAL$! Farewell to arms!\n\nDemonstrations broke out across $COUNTRYNAME$. Demonstrators demanded an end to hostilities and a peace agreement with our enemies. Our country is built on a fundamental truth: all men are created equal. This group of demonstrators sees themselves as part of a larger whole, and they don't even exclude our country's enemies from this whole.

As the great powers contend for control over our country's politics, our independence is increasingly weakened and gradually becoming a mere formality. Recently, a case that occurred on $COUNTRY_ADJ$ territory caused the great powers to argue endlessly over criminal investigation jurisdiction, with the situation threatening to escalate. If the great powers don't insist on their respective positions, they can only lose influence.

In $FROMCOUNTRY$, our country is at odds with other great powers over criminal investigation issues, and tensions are on the verge of breaking out. Our position is that we have the right to conduct our own criminal investigations in $FROMCOUNTRY$ without interference from local or foreign governments. This position has been clearly opposed by our rivals. Our options here are either to uphold our position (which would be seen as a further erosion of $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ independence) or to retreat (representing a loss of influence in $FROMCOUNTRY$).

Even among the great powers of the world, our country has established a formidable reputation. From $CAPITAL$ to distant border provinces, our flag flies proudly in the wind, striking fear into the hearts of anyone who dares to oppose us. An imperial parade celebrating our just rule is being prepared in $CAPITAL$. The question now arises: should we invite those foreign dignitaries to this festive occasion, or simply conclude that no other country deserves to bask in the sun with us?
Let the world witness our country's glory!

The flora of $PROVINCENAME$ is unique and breathtaking, and the scientific community still knows very little about it. Here, in this mysterious land not even marked on maps, immeasurable botanical treasures are waiting to be discovered by any explorer who dares to face the harsh and unforgiving climate. The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Botanical Society is considering sending an expedition to $PROVINCENAME$, but as is usually the case with such matters, they lack funds. While sending an expedition can advance scientific causes, we must also be wary of possible competition.
We have more important things to do

Rumor has it that $FROMCOUNTRY$ has sent a botanical expedition to $FROMPROVINCE$. From the rumors, $FROMPROVINCE$'s flora is truly a treasure trove of beauty and biodiversity. Although $FROMPROVINCE$ is a $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ colony, we can still try to send our own expedition. Things may not be easy, but the mere possibility of discovery is already extraordinarily tempting.

The botanical expedition we sent not long ago is stranded in Marrakech, with a leaking ship and lacking supplies. The captain of the expedition sent back a boat with a message requesting additional funds to continue their journey into the heart of darkness. Should we provide more funds?
The scientific cause needs that money

...While some of our people at home cannot even meet their basic needs for food and clothing, our government is spending millions to send an expedition to a godforsaken corner looking for flowers!\n\nOur earlier funding of the botanical expedition has now triggered a debate in the House of Lords. The liberals oppose the subsidy for the expedition, claiming that $COUNTRYNAME$ cannot afford such a luxurious investment.

...So far, our expedition has newly catalogued 20 previously undiscovered plant species. Two more people have fallen ill in the stench of malaria and dysentery in the past month, but despite the loss of friends, our team's morale remains high. With best wishes and love, signed...\n\nThe expedition we sent has reported back. Obviously, as research deepens, they need more support.
Let's see if they can find anything edible themselves

The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ botanical expedition that was sent earlier has not been heard from for a long time. Recently, we received a distressing message:

"The camp has been abandoned. Signs of struggle were found around the original camp site. The trail extends into the vast and unfriendly unknown territory. I think this is the final fate of the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ botanical expedition in $YEAR$."

It seems our expedition has disappeared.

The botanical expedition we sent earlier brought back a new species of flower. This flower, about the size of an adult's fist, quickly became the talk of Europe, and gardeners across the country are eager to cultivate it. To commemorate our significant investment, this flower was named "Empress Flower." Our scientific discovery has earned us envious looks from around the world.

$FROMCOUNTRY$ claims that the famous white flower recently discovered will henceforth be known to the world as "Empress Flower." In the glow of this significant discovery, our expedition is unlikely to find results that can rival the $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ discovery. With limited results, our expedition returned home.

Today, the streets of the capital $CAPITAL$ are covered with flowers to celebrate the return of the $YEAR$ botanical expedition. The expedition achieved world-shocking results, discovering over a hundred new plant species in the colonial flora. Our country can be proud of this, and these discoveries help advance the scientific cause!

With the decline of the Ottoman Empire, people began to mock this once-powerful nation as the "Sick Man of Europe." Nationalism and unrest in non-Turkish provinces became a headache for the Ottoman Empire, and with the empire being more backward than Western countries, many believed its destruction was only a matter of time. Meanwhile, the Ottoman Empire's cruel treatment of Christians led $FROMCOUNTRY$ to claim that it would be the protector of Orthodox Christians. Should we recognize $FROMCOUNTRY$'s challenge to Ottoman authority?

$FROMCOUNTRY$ rejected our claimed title—the supreme authority and protector of Orthodox Christians within the Ottoman Empire. We can continue to exercise our rights despite $FROMCOUNTRY$'s opposition, but this would be seen as a reasonable pretext for $FROMCOUNTRY$ to launch war. If we lose this war, we will lose the rights we possess.
If that's the case, then forget it

$FROMCOUNTRY$ firmly claims to be the "defender of Orthodox Christians within the Ottoman Empire." We now have a reasonable pretext to declare war on them, and if we win the war, they will lose this right.
$FROMCOUNTRY$ announced the renunciation of its claim to be the "defender of Orthodox Christians within the Ottoman Empire." This means the possibility of war over this dispute has been avoided.

As tensions over the Eastern Question continue to rise, regarding who will be the legitimate protector of Christians within the Ottoman Empire, we can choose to form an alliance with other countries on this issue. Should we do this?
$FROMCOUNTRY$ proposes establishing a broad alliance to protect Ottoman territory from violation. Joining this alliance may mean war. Which side will you stand on?
No, we can resolve this ourselves.

$FROMCOUNTRY$ has raised a demand for excavation rights in the Valley of the Kings. Given that we currently have neither the ability nor the funds to excavate the area, allowing foreign contractors may make sense. However, we could also leave our country's proud history undisturbed until we have the ability to excavate it ourselves, which would be the best approach. But refusing would damage our relations with foreign powers.
The Valley of the Kings is ours

The Egyptian government has granted our country exclusive rights to excavate and investigate the ancient sites in the Valley of the Kings. The potential discoveries here will give us an excellent opportunity to improve our reputation in the scientific field.
The Egyptian government refused to grant our country excavation rights to the Valley of the Kings. Our international reputation has been damaged, and relations with Egypt have been strained.

Egyptian officials in Alexandria refused to allow our Egyptian expedition to unload its excavation equipment at the port. Egypt's Byzantine-style customs system cannot be smoothly passed through without personal connections and money. Although we can pressure the Egyptian government, it would certainly be best if the expedition could bribe its way through.

Our archaeological expedition discovered an Eighteenth Dynasty tomb in the Valley of the Kings in Egypt. The entire tomb is rectangular, divided into upper and lower parts, with the royal sarcophagus placed in the lower part. This outstanding discovery has made our Egyptian research department the center of attention of historical circles throughout Europe!

No one knows how it started, we only know that what was once a mere rumor has now become a socially recognized truth. The rumor grew from nothing into a terrifying storm, claiming that anyone who dares to disturb the pharaoh's tomb in the Valley of the Kings will be cursed by the pharaoh. Some even claim that the expedition will bring a curse upon the entire $COUNTRY$. Although this is certainly just a crazy rumor, madness has become reality.
What will come next? A comet's omen?

...Opening the internal granite lid and heading deeper into the tomb, I breathed air that had not been disturbed for three thousand years. As far as I know, I was the first person to disturb the pharaoh's rest since he was buried here thousands of years ago. Here, in this ancient and mysterious atmosphere, I seemed to smell the wheat along the Nile, the perfume in the gypsum bottles, and the faint smell of decayed papyrus.\n\n$COUNTRY_ADJ$ archaeologists working in the Valley of the Kings have achieved the most astonishing discovery of the century: the previously undiscovered tomb of the 19-year-old pharaoh Tutankhamun.

Our expedition working in the Valley of the Kings discovered an as-yet-undiscovered tomb containing the mummy of a high priest from the Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt. The tomb's interior is very elaborately decorated, which is a major discovery for our expedition.

His Majesty the King has again refused to receive the ambassador, and later sent an adjutant to inform us that the King does not intend to continue contact with the ambassador.\n\nThe French ambassador was snubbed by the Prussian King at the royal resort of Bad Ems (in Hesse-Nassau, Prussia), leading to a diplomatic conflict between France and Germany. Rumor has it that this dispatch may have been a deliberate move by German officials to provoke war.
This is really a dirty trick...

Keep, ancient lands, your storied pomp! cries she with silent lips. "Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free..."\n\nThe French people gave a special gift to the American people. A colossal bronze statue, 151 feet tall, depicting a woman holding a torch, was named "Liberty Enlightening the World." Designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, a small island next to New York Harbor has been prepared for the statue's placement. This statue will henceforth be known as the "Statue of Liberty."
I lift my lamp beside the golden door

Our scouts discovered some wreckage near the Boshiman River a few days ago—a still-smoldering covered wagon of pioneers. From the tracks, it was determined that this was the result of an attack, and we also found some body remains. Obviously, this family of South African whites met with misfortune. The residual arrows nearby tell us that a Zulu armed team from our southeast appears to be responsible for this massacre.
They won't get away with this!

Through our Cape colony, a large number of colonists headed to the newly incorporated town of "Johannesburg," surging towards the edges of the Witwatersrand Mountains in a massive gold rush. The influx of foreign residents into this region has caused trouble along our borders, but this may be a good pretext for us to end the independence of these annoying nations on the fringes.

Tuberculosis was one of the most common killers of the 19th century. This contagious disease usually targets the human lungs. Today we know tuberculosis is caused by bacteria, but historical explanations for tuberculosis varied, from vampires to imbalances in "basic fluids." Although tuberculosis has been known since ancient times, it was not until 1020 that Avicenna confirmed it as a contagious disease transmitted through contact. Typical symptoms of this disease include chronic cough, fever, and bloody sputum. In the 19th century, because several famous writers and poets of the era were sufferers, this disease sometimes took on romantic overtones.

Although plague and large-scale famine have almost disappeared with the modernization, capitalization, development of free market systems and hired labor divisions in the Western world, as one of humanity's oldest killers, starvation still causes much suffering in the 20th century. Of course, only among the poor classes. Famine has struck a region of our country, and we need to respond immediately.
We must help these starving people!
Sorry, I've referred this to the office.

The most common way typhoid fever spreads is through contaminated water or food. Due to the lack of healthcare systems, crowded living conditions, and lack of public health facilities, typhoid fever became one of the major killers of the 19th century. In Chicago in 1891, 174 out of every 10,000 people died from typhoid fever. This disease usually starts with a low-grade fever, gradually manifests through weeks of internal bleeding and neurological confusion, and may eventually lead to death. With improvements in hygiene, many developed countries have more or less eradicated this disease. However, in $YEAR$, at least one $COUNTRY_ADJ$ region has been severely hit by the epidemic.

Spanish flu spread widely between 1918 and 1920 and caused approximately 50 million to 100 million deaths worldwide. Due to increasing trade in the 19th century, colonial development, commercial activities, and other activities that brought the world closer together, Spanish flu could rapidly spread around the world within a few years. Combined with the ongoing World War I and crowded living conditions, Spanish flu became the first and most terrifying example of a global pandemic. And... think about it... do you feel a bit feverish?
Use every possible means to fight this disease
This isn't true, why would this happen?

In the 18th century, smallpox, a highly pathogenic malignant epidemic caused by the smallpox virus, caused 400,000 deaths in Europe annually. Successful vaccination programs in the 19th and 20th centuries eventually systematically eradicated this disease under the leadership of the World Health Organization in 1979, but this is only a small comfort to the people living in $YEAR$ in your region where smallpox rages.
Fight the plague with all possible means. Every life is precious!
We are powerless against it, you understand?

The huge fireball produced by the 1908 Tunguska explosion destroyed large areas of forest and also caused widespread shaking around the world. Scientists believe this explosion was caused by a meteorite or asteroid impact.

The volcanic eruption of Krakatoa and the resulting tsunami caused 36,500 deaths in the Dutch East Indies. The sound of the eruption could even be heard on Rodriguez Island in the Indian Ocean, 3,000 miles away. The eruption had astonishing global effects: the volcanic ash dispersed around the world causing years of dim skies, while producing intense red sunsets and other optical effects, which caused a 1-degree Celsius drop in global average temperatures.

Today a violent earthquake struck San Francisco and the entire California region, causing widespread destruction and thousands of deaths. The shock was clearly felt as far away as Nevada, and the earthquake also caused severe fires. The military is fully transporting supplies to survivors, and it is believed this earthquake will leave a deep psychological imprint on an entire generation.

The trusty system originated in Mississippi, USA, and was later adopted by Alabama, Texas, Louisiana, and several other states. Well-behaved prisoners (usually those willing to follow orders) were allowed to guard other prisoners in the prison under a strict military-style hierarchical system, and some especially trustworthy prisoners were even allowed to carry weapons. The profits from prisoner labor were the cornerstone of this system. The system first originated at the end of the 19th century and the beginning of the 20th century at Parchman Farm Prison in Mississippi, and was praised as the most modern criminal reform system. A large number of prisoner abuse reports around 1970 led to the end of this system, but in $YEAR$, it was a fashionable system in many parts of $COUNTRY$.
Spare the rod and spoil the child!

The idea of separating criminals from society may be as old as our history itself. Many classical legal systems used exile as a final disposal method, which for serious criminals was even more painful than death. With the growth of European colonial empires from the 18th to the 19th century, this idea was inherited in the form of penal colonies, as in the famous (or rather infamous) British Botany Bay colony and the French "Devil's Island" in French Guiana. Since $COUNTRY$ has occupied some areas very suitable as penal colonies, perhaps we should consider establishing such a social system ourselves?
No one can escape from Azazel's atoll!
I think we should adopt a more humane approach
Since we no longer have areas suitable for exiling criminals, our penal colony system has been abolished.
Well, good, it should be done this way

Two filthy day rooms and three unpleasant night rooms. Eight square feet for men, one room for women is eight to nine square feet, the rest are only 4.5 square feet. Straw on the ground, worn and dusty, filled with all kinds of pests. No yard, no water for prisoners. Poor prisoners wearing iron shackles. Until my last inspection, there were still eight female prisoners.
—John Howard

In $COUNTRY$, people organized the Penal Reform League to protest the terrible prison conditions, criminal rehabilitation facilities, and related systems in the country. The league proposed single cells for use in prisons and other ideas aimed at improving their crowded living conditions.
Prisons are supposed to be dirty, dear.
There are some reform measures worth considering.
We must first ensure we hold a majority in the upper house

News of a despicable murder shocked $COUNTRY$. A young prostitute was brutally killed by a client, and it is said that because the murderer came from a prominent local banking family, the police covered up his identity. Nevertheless, the police repeatedly stated that the incident is still under investigation and the murderer has not yet been found. Everyone is talking about this matter, so much so that it has alerted parliament, and liberal members demanded that the government clarify the matter.
Demand the police find the murderer
Let's not make unfounded wild accusations.

They march in narrow alleys, carrying iron chains wherever they go. They are not slaves, but criminals who have been fairly sentenced by the court to perform hard labor and sweat under the sun. Such people are often seen in $COUNTRY$, many like them. In $COUNTRY$'s courts, forced labor has long been a common punishment. Hard labor is believed to improve the moral consciousness of these fools. Therefore, they need to work.
We need to consider using more humane punishments

As police announced that a convicted murderer had escaped from a local prison, a region-wide manhunt was launched in one part of our country. While this news is disturbing in itself, it has also drawn public attention to our country's prison system, thereby exacerbating national debate on crime and punishment. Liberals believe this escape is a further silent indictment of the tragic state of our country's prison system, while conservatives claim the matter is caused by natural constraints on the national budget and that we should not spend more money on what could be called our worst citizens.

And then we have this guy. He started like everyone else, feeling uneasy, but it didn't take long before he was on his way to robbing a bank. He will spend the rest of his life here, so we make him wear chains most of the time. I think this will drive him mad in a few years, if he isn't already.\n\nLife imprisonment without parole is not a very unusual punishment in $COUNTRY$, nevertheless, in some liberal circles, there has been debate about the nature of crime and punishment, and the argument has been made that using instruments like chains and inhumane treatment deprives prisoners of the ability to reform. A movement demanding improvements in prison laws is brewing.
This issue can certainly be considered
I think we should continue using the old methods

As Europe entered the 19th century, the phenomenon of people being imprisoned for debt remained common. In Britain, "debtors' prisons" including Fleet Prison in London were representatives of such facilities. Here, debtors were not only required to pay for accommodation and meals, but sometimes even had to pay "guard fees" to cover the guard's salary. Usually, these measures only worsened the debtor's economic situation, for the simple reason that people couldn't raise money in prison. Most European countries abolished such systems in the 19th century, and London's Fleet Prison was closed in 1846. A group of wrongly imprisoned $COUNTRY_ADJ$ nobles are seeking more public attention for this facility, calling for its abolition.
This issue should be carefully considered
This doesn't convince me. People need to learn lessons in life

People debated the death penalty at the Reform Club in $CAPITAL$ tonight, and the arguments of death penalty opponents have further developed. The argument focuses on the irreversibility of punishment and the ever-present risk of wrongful sentencing. Liberals gathered together to form a citizens' committee demanding the abolition of this punishment. The debate was triggered by the execution of an old man who was clearly in the late stages of dementia, but was sentenced to death for murdering his wife. A newly formed group is calling on its members' parliamentary representatives to stand up against what they consider the most terrible and unjust legal provision, and they have found a cabinet member to represent their position.
Of course I'd be happy to meet with them
I don't have time to listen to the liberals' arrogant nonsense!

Mom, Mom! Old Johnson brought back a new machine! It can plow, haul, move, and you can even sit on it! He said it's called a 'tractor'!\n\nThe appearance of the tractor in $PROVINCENAME$ triggered a local agricultural revolution, making agricultural production scale far exceed that of the previous generation. In fact, industrial development has brought tremendous benefits to $COUNTRY$.

Mom, Mom! Did you see the lights on the street? They're replacing the old street lamps! They say these new lamps use 'electricity' as energy!\n\nElectricity, in the form of street lamps, came to $PROVINCENAME$. This new type of light illuminating our city had only appeared in dreams before, and electricity has improved local industrial production efficiency and quality of life.

Mom, Mom! Did you hear the sound of explosives from the mine? They say it's a new type of explosive!\n\nThe introduced nitroglycerin allows us to dig deeper mines than ever before, meaning a several-fold increase in mining output in $PROVINCENAME$.

Mom! Mom! A new shop opened in town!\n\nThe 19th century witnessed rapid development of commodity distribution channels, which broadly expanded new customer groups. Brand new, more specialized, industrialized retailers brought new types of industrial products to consumers. The newly opened shop in $PROVINCENAME$ will promote local agricultural production, so farmers don't have to spend a lot of time on transportation and organizing markets.

Mom! Mom! Dad says they're using new tools in the mine!\n\nWith the invention of mechanized mining tools, mines gradually switched to new and more efficient mining tools to develop deeper mineral resources. Therefore, the mineral industry in $PROVINCENAME$ has made great progress.
Nevertheless, let's not be too greedy and mine too deep.

Archaeologist Heinrich Schliemann discovered the lost city of Troy in Turkey! This astonishing discovery caused a huge stir in archaeological circles and simultaneously triggered countless associations.
In January 1837, Switzerland conducted its first official census. The results indicated that the total population of Switzerland was 2,190,258.
France Requests Extradition of Louis Napoleon

In August 1838, the French government requested the extradition of Louis Napoleon (nephew of Emperor Napoleon I), who claimed to be the heir to the French throne, from Switzerland. The Swiss refused extradition, and a seemingly inevitable French invasion was avoided when Louis Napoleon went to London.
In 1852, telegraph technology based on the Morse system was introduced to Switzerland. Initially, 27 telegraph stations were established in this mountainous country.
New era of communication in Switzerland
The public voice has been heard.
The just-concluded referendum shows that the people agree to the nationalization of railways.
The just-concluded referendum shows that the people agree to grant Jews full citizenship rights in Switzerland.
The just-concluded referendum shows that the people agree to state monopoly on alcohol sales.
Coup by Radical Liberals in Ticino

A bloody coup by radical liberals broke out in Ticino, but was subsequently crushed by federal troops. This incident heightened tensions between the conflicting parties, but the acquittal of the coup leaders also convinced reactionaries that the government was working against them.
Order must be restored in Ticino.
Empress Elizabeth of Austria, von Wittelsbach, was assassinated by Italian anarchist Luigi Lucheni. This terrifying scene occurred at the Beau-Rivage Hotel in Geneva.

On September 4, 1915, the Socialist International held a meeting at Zimmerwald, the first since the outbreak of World War I in August 1914. Although the previous Socialist International meeting held in Brazil in November 1912 had raised the possibility of using this brewing war as an opportunity to overthrow capitalist rule. The meeting delegates condemned the terrible casualties caused by the imperialist war and called on the working class to rise up against the spread of war. Many famous socialist movement leaders attended this meeting, including Italy's Lazzari and Modigliani, Russia's Lenin and Bobrow, Germany's Ledebour and Hoffmann, and French socialists Bourderon and Merrheim.
A socialist congress was held at Kiental. Many socialist movement leaders attended and discussed different methods of building an ideal socialist paradise.
16 countries signed the Geneva Convention to help soldiers wounded in battle. They chose the reversed Swiss flag as their symbol: a red cross on a white background.
This idea should have been realized long ago

Pushkin, one of the most influential writers in contemporary Russian literature and the literary master who led Russia to catch up with other European countries, is known for Eugene Onegin, Boris Godunov, and The Captain's Daughter. He died in February 1837 after a duel with a French exile.
This is truly a tragic death
The Polish Independence Committee was established in Paris, aiming to help Poland gain independence from the control of Russia, Austro-Hungary, and Prussia.
What do you want? Poland shouldn't be on the map.

Founded in 1844, the Petrashevsky Circle was dedicated to reforming Tsarist Russia. Its members included the famous Fyodor Dostoevsky. In May 1849, 123 members were arrested, most were shot, and Dostoevsky himself was exiled to Siberia.

Located in St. Petersburg, the Hermitage was designed and built by Leo von Klenze, and its art collections have been opened to the public. This gives the public the opportunity to see the finest and most precious art collections in all of Russia.

On February 8, 1874, after years of preparation, Mussorgsky's opera "Boris Godunov" was finally unveiled and performed for the first time. The opera sought to fuse the ideas of Richard Wagner with Russian folk music, striving to present truly Russian national music.

In 1880, Dostoevsky completed his masterpiece "The Brothers Karamazov." As one of the most celebrated works in literary history, "The Brothers Karamazov" became an important landmark in Dostoevsky's writing career after the failure of his socialist movement. Although it is a comedic work, it can be said to be the most serious comedy in history. In his autobiographical "Writer's Diary," Dostoevsky refuted the criticism by leftists of the chapters "Rebellion" and "The Grand Inquisitor" in his work "The Brothers Karamazov" on the grounds that "the left has never intentionally damaged Christian tradition." Dostoevsky's works had a profound influence not only in Russia but also throughout the West, and also caused strong repercussions in literary, philosophical, and religious circles.
Sometimes two plus two equals five.
In 1837, a railway with a total length of 26 kilometers connecting St. Petersburg and the royal residence at Tsarskoye Selo was completed. This was the first railway in the Russian Empire.

The first official treaty signed between Russia and Japan was called the "Treaty of Friendship, Trade, and Boundaries." On February 7, 1855, the treaty was signed by Russian Navy Vice Admiral Putyatin in Shimoda, Japan. The treaty stipulated that the Northern Kuril Islands would become part of Russia, while Sakhalin Island would be "jointly" administered by both countries. At the same time, Japan agreed to open three ports to Russian trade.
We will trade with the Japanese!
The successful performance style of Chekhov's "The Seagull" showed that the Moscow Art Theater was the best representative to lead Russian theater into the 20th century.
The troupe from the Duchy of Saxe-Meiningen received rave reviews after performing in Berlin. They will soon begin their tour of European countries.

In 1874, Carl Hagenbeck, a livestock dealer's son, held his first show displaying foreign customs in Hamburg. In 1887, he broke conventions and established a circus that trained animals without force. Eventually in 1907, Hagenbeck unveiled his zoo in Hamburg, which became a leader among similar zoos.
Lions, zebras, and elephants for everyone to see!

In 1880, Konrad Duden, then a school director, published his first complete German dictionary. For many years it was the basic standard for German orthography and remains the most authoritative German dictionary to this day.
Finally, the language has a unified standard.

In 1903, the Baghdad Railway, funded by Germany and connecting Constantinople with Baghdad, was proposed as a plan. This marked the arrival of a new peak in friendly diplomatic relations between Constantinople and Berlin.
This has nothing to do with us.
A three-day fire reduced nearly one-third of Hamburg to ashes. This serious disaster led to fire safety system reforms and more planned urban development.

The Austria of the Hamburg-America Line (HAPAG) sank off the coast of Newfoundland. The accident was caused by using smoke to disinfect the hold, when a hot chain accidentally dipped into a tar barrel. The overheated chain burned the boatswain, then fell to the ground, instantly igniting a fire. The accident caused 495 passenger deaths, most of whom were immigrants from Europe.

Major merchants in Hamburg established the "Hamburg-Amerikanische Packetfahrt Actiengesellschaft" (Hamburg-America Packet Shipping Company). The company provided transatlantic shipping services, which was welcomed by the growing number of immigrants to America.

After the death of Duke William of Brunswick-Lüneburg without any suitable heir, Ernst August II, as his closest cousin, was successfully enfeoffed as the new Duke of Brunswick. Therefore, the duchy became part of my kingdom.
We are now part of Hanover

In 1838, 42 choirs from the Rhineland, Baden, Hesse, and Franconia participated in a three-day festival in Frankfurt commemorating Mozart. However, this event turned into a demonstration demanding German unification.
They should come to sing, not to argue!
Puccini Adapts American Drama into Italian Opera
Peter II Officially Becomes Grand Duke!
When Oldenburg was elevated from a duchy to a grand duchy on June 9, 1815, His Majesty Peter II officially assumed the title of Grand Duke as the first ruler.
Diesterweg Publishes "Guide for German Teacher Training"
German educator Adolf Diesterweg proposed educational principles aimed at making children self-aware, thoughtful, and responsible citizens. His views once caused him to be suspended in 1847.
This is an interesting idea anyway!

In August 1841, Hoffmann von Fallersleben created his poem "Deutschlandlied" on the island of Heligoland. The "Deutschlandlied," combined with the melody of Joseph Haydn's "God Save Franz the Emperor," would one day become the German national anthem.
On June 7, 1840, King Frederick William III passed away at the age of 70. His son, with a touch of romantic thought, inherited the throne.
In August 1844, Berlin witnessed the opening of the first zoo in German history. At that time, London and Antwerp already had similar zoos.
In October 1845, newly promulgated Prussian laws stipulated that Jews must have fixed surnames. Now they also have the obligation to serve in the military.
All our citizens have equal obligations!
Prussian astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle discovered Neptune. This would be the latest planet discovered in the solar system until 1930.
The comic opera "The Merry Wives of Windsor," based on the Shakespearean play of the same name, premiered in Berlin, and it would become the pinnacle of Nicolai's career.
I don't know, I prefer serious drama.
The Krupp Company in Essen established a medical insurance fund for 970 workers. Participation in insurance was mandatory.
Extend this measure to the whole country!
In 1839, Prussia, following the British example, passed laws limiting the number of child workers, pushed by religious and social figures.
In 1837, Albert Lortzing's most well-known opera "Zar und Zimmermann" (Tsar and Carpenter) premiered in Leipzig. Lortzing is regarded as the father of German comic opera (similar to romantic opera).

Saxon court architect Professor Gottfried Semper completed a masterpiece—the Dresden Opera House, which would become known by its designer's name. Semper's style was influenced by both classical and Renaissance styles, and it is not only because of his works that Dresden earned the reputation as "Florence on the Elbe."

Giacomo Puccini successfully adapted the American playwright David Belasco's play "Madame Butterfly" into an opera in 1904. Now another work of his has premiered, based on Belasco's "The Girl of the Golden West," called "The Girl of the Golden West."
Enrico Caruso's performance in "Rigoletto" in London earned him international fame.
Verdi's most influential work "Nabucco" premiered at La Scala in Milan, captivating the hearts of many Italians. The prisoner chorus in it became Italy's unofficial national anthem.

Pope Leo XIII began his encyclical on labor issues with "Rerum Novarum" (Of New Things). The encyclical analyzed that the mutable spirit of socialist revolution had begun to prevail in various regions. It stated that the causes of the dispute are "obvious: namely, the development of industry
column3: the astonishing discoveries of science
column4: the changes in relations between employers and employees
column5: the immense wealth of a few individuals and the poverty of the masses
column6: the growing self-assertion of the laboring class and their increasing mutual solidarity
column7: and finally, the general moral decay." The encyclical pointed out that socialism threatened the religious and moral foundations of the state and attempted to destroy the common interests of the Church, the state, employers, and employees, replacing them with the heresy of atheism. To counter this threat, it was necessary to establish organizations capable of meeting the needs of progress and protecting the poor and helpless. The encyclical quoted the words of the Apostle Paul: "Charity is patient, is kind... seeks not its own... endures all things... perseveres in all things."

column2: The value of labor and wealth are equal.

Edvard Munch (1863-1944) had a major influence on the growth of Expressionism. His works so shocked the upper classes that they were initially banned. His works raised awareness of the terrible conditions in society.

Farmer's son and teacher Ivar Aasen (1813-1896) believed that the Norwegian written language, which had been Danish until now, needed reform. Through several journeys across villages and farms, he created new grammar and a dictionary of a "new" Norwegian language. Although his compilation of spoken language and grammar did not do much for people's education, many of his poems became songs spread throughout the countryside. Just before his death, his new language was officially recognized by the Norwegian parliament.
A people's language for the whole nation

Norway at the end of the 19th century was shaken by the works of several famous writers: Henrik Ibsen, Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson, Alexander Kielland, and Jonas Lie. Their realistic novels and plays angered those in power, aroused widespread nationwide discussion, and paved the way for large-scale social reform.

In 1884, Johan Sverdrup of the liberal faction demanded in the Norwegian parliament that the basis of the government should be the parliamentary majority. Although never passed in the form of a law or decree, this became a legitimate precedent, and the Norwegian parliament began to unite along party lines to oppose the king.

Marcus Thrane, inspired by the revolutionary sentiments of Europe in 1848, established a union. They demanded full suffrage, improved conditions for guarantors, and the abolition of all tariffs on imported grain. The government suppressed this movement, and Thrane was sentenced to 5 years in prison.

Swedish soprano Jenny Lind was born in Stockholm in 1820. She made her debut in the opera "Der Freischütz" in Stockholm in 1838, and her reputation spread far and wide in the 1840s due to a series of successful performances in Europe and the United States. Jenny Lind was the first Swedish performing superstar, known for her round and emotional voice, incredible singing technique, and sincere, natural, and humble demeanor. Although she earned wealth through concerts and opera performances, she donated most of it to charitable causes.

In 1842, Sweden officially introduced compulsory elementary education. Although there had already been traditional education, the "1842 Compulsory Elementary Education Act" virtually eliminated illiteracy among the younger generation. Local towns and parishes now had the means to force reluctant parents to fulfill their obligation to educate children of school age.

The first "Aftonbladet" (Evening Paper) was edited by Lars Johan Hierta and published on Monday, December 6, 1830. The newspaper supported freedom of speech, free trade, lower import tariffs, and democratic reform, which made it unpopular with the government. The newspaper was despised by the nobility but loved by the middle class, and despite the king's attempts to ban its publication, its circulation surged in the following years. As the voice of liberalism, the "Aftonbladet" became a cornerstone of Sweden's battle for freedom of speech.

Europe's year of 1848 was one of revolution and unrest. On March 19, 1848, tensions finally spread to Sweden, and a large crowd with discontent and rebellious hearts took to the streets of Stockholm. People from various ideologies and all classes joined the protest. The mob rampaged through the city, destroying property and attacking anyone they disliked. King Oscar I personally tried to turn the mob around, but soon the mob went to another part of the city to cause destruction.
Goran Fredrik Goransson Introduces Bessemer's Method

Goran Fredrik Goransson was the first person to successfully introduce the Englishman Henry Bessemer's steelmaking method on an industrial scale. This method was a converter steelmaking process that blew air through bottom tuyeres to directly convert molten iron into steel. His success allowed a new steel mill to be established in Sandviken, which became the predecessor of the famous Sandvik Group.
Our scientists have driven the country's development

In the mid-1860s, the agricultural sector fell into difficulties after a series of poor harvests. The difficulties persisted until 1867, when crops failed again. During these years known as "The Wet Year," grain generally rotted due to dampness, causing famine in many parts of the country.

After the previous disastrous harvests caused by excessive rain, there was another harvest failure in 1868. This time it was a year of high temperatures and drought, and some fields caught fire. Famine struck many places, and many families began emigrating abroad.

Difficulties continued in 1869. Infectious diseases broke out, famine spread everywhere in cities and countryside, and people begged due to despair. Emigration abroad increased dramatically, with over 60,000 people leaving Sweden during the three famine years of 1867-69.
A spectacular ceremony was held in Arvika in 1871 to celebrate the official connection of the national railway networks of Sweden and Norway.

A small island called Saint Barthélemy in the West Indies was ruled by Sweden for 94 years until it was decided to sell it to France in 1878. The island no longer enjoyed the prosperity it had as a free port during the revolutions and Napoleonic wars of previous decades, and now it had become an economic burden.
For the glory of Sweden, we must keep it!

In 1879, the Swedish economy was sluggish, and sawmill employers in Sundsvall were forced to cut wages. A spontaneous and organized strike broke out and spread to 21 different sawmills, with 6,000 workers participating. This was the first large-scale strike in Swedish history. The strike united workers, was an early starting point of the working class and social democratic movement, and became the precursor to the flourishing trade union organizations in the following decades.
Please don't forget law and order!

August Strindberg (1849-1912) was one of the world-famous literary giants. He was a playwright, novelist, and short story writer, and his works showed a combination of frenzy and genius, incorporating naturalism, psychology, and mysticism. "The Red Room" in 1879 made him famous overnight. The novel satirized the institutions and environment of Sweden in the late 1870s. Strindberg was a complex figure: he had an almost mad hatred for women, he was simultaneously interested in science and mysticism, and he even tried painting, photography, and alchemy!

In 1900, the Swedish parliament decided to build a vast fortification system in Boden near the Finnish border. The fortress was built on the top of a rocky hill, located by the Lule River in a strategically important position, with a stunningly wide field of view. The purpose of the fortress was to guard the country's northern flank and local natural resources against the threat of Russian invasion.
Yes, our defenses must be strong!
No, now is not the time

Carl Jonas Love Almqvist was a famous Swedish writer with a complex personality, who produced a large body of prose with romantic, mystical, and social consciousness. He had an important influence on the development of Swedish literature. In his work "Det går an" (It's Acceptable), he challenged traditional views on marriage and the status of women in society. The book caused a social debate upon its release.
Agricultural Depression Leads to Mass Emigration

1880 was a difficult period for the agricultural sector, and combined with growing population and discontent, these problems led to large-scale emigration. Over the decade, families emigrated at an alarming rate. More than 340,000 people went to America, where wider lands and greater opportunities beckoned them.
Louis de Geer Promotes Parliamentary Reform

The ancient Swedish parliamentary system contained four estates: nobility, clergy, burghers, and peasants. Recently, Louis de Geer proposed replacing the old system with two chambers with equal power in parliament. Although this was a liberal reform, democracy was still far away. The new system was unfair, and voting rights would be controlled by wealthy merchants. The reform proposal sparked a nationwide movement demanding universal suffrage for men and women.
No, we must keep the four estates!
King Charles John of Sweden and Norway conceded to the demands of the Swedish parliament, allowing Norwegian ships to fly the Norwegian flag in all waters.

Denmark's victory in the First Schleswig War saw many Scandinavian volunteers participate, which was the sprout of the Scandinavian movement. Later, many student meetings were held, the largest of which was one held in Uppsala in 1856.
The Wife of Raja Mohan Published
Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay published the first Bengali novel.
The Indian people have their own voice!
Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General of India, implemented a series of reform measures in India. Although the reforms were unpopular in some areas, they were effective.
Our mission in India requires us to reform!
Don't stir up a hornet's nest.

A treaty formally establishing the national status of New Zealand was signed, in which the Maori chiefs acknowledged the sovereignty of Queen Victoria, and the queen guaranteed their land, property, and fishing rights in return.
Maori chief Hone Heke cut down the flagpole several times at Kororareka despite British attitudes to protest.
We must catch this chief in the act
What can we do about this situation?

Any veteran who wants to emigrate to New Zealand can get free passage to New Zealand, a cottage, and a pension, as long as they attend church, march in parades, and train with the militia for twelve days a year.

The head of the Bonaparte family is an outspoken critic of our regime, and he has currently obtained asylum in Switzerland, where he is inciting our subjects to challenge our authority. Should we demand that the Swiss extradite him?
Let him roam the Alps, he's no threat anyway

The Paris Arc de Triomphe was originally commissioned by Napoleon Bonaparte and completed in 1836 after 30 years of on-and-off construction. The monument was inspired by Roman triumphal arches, and the scenes carved on it depict the victories of the French Revolutionary Wars and Napoleon's achievements.
The July Column was unveiled in Paris in 1840, commemorating the 615 dead of the July Revolution of 1830.
Charles Louis-Napoléon, nephew of Napoleon I, launched an unsuccessful seizure of power in Boulogne.

In 1821, Napoleon Bonaparte died on Saint Helena, and his remains were returned to France in 1840. Several days after the funeral held at the Les Invalides church in Paris, thousands of people paid their respects to him.
French balloonist Francois Arban became the first person to cross the Alps in a balloon. He departed from Marseille and landed at Stupini.
Belgian instrument maker Adolphe Sax registered a patent for an instrument called the "saxophone." However, his French competitor took him to court, preventing him from marketing his invention.
Louis-Napoléon Bonaparte, nephew of Napoleon I, was sentenced to life imprisonment in the fortress at Ham following the failed coup in 1840. However, in May 1846 he managed to escape to England.
After the February Revolution of 1848, King Louis-Philippe of France abdicated, and Louis-Napoléon, nephew of Napoleon I, was elected President of the Republic.
At a planetarium in Paris, French physicist Léon Foucault demonstrated that the Earth rotates on its axis. His experiment was repeated at the Panthéon in Paris, astonishing the audience present.
In July 1851, Proudhon published "General Idea of the Revolution in the Nineteenth Century," establishing the foundation of anarchist thought.
Pioneer Henry Giffard flew a dirigible (a balloon powered by a small engine) alone from Versailles to Trappes, a distance of 27 kilometers, shocking all observers.
On May 15, 1855, the World's Fair was held in Paris. 20,839 exhibitors displayed their products, received 11,073 awards in total, and attracted 4.5 million visitors.

In 1835, Alexis de Tocqueville published his work "Democracy in America," which was soon regarded as a classic in both the United States and France. In the book, he commented on Americans' love of litigation and devotion to religion, some of which still puzzle Europeans today. Tocqueville is one of the few historians who has more than one "classic" work to his name.
